title: US loses measles elimination status as health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr faces pressure
content:
The United States has lost its measles elimination status, an official designation that the disease was no longer endemic after 26 years of elimination. The loss comes amid the worst measles outbreak in the country since 1991.

In a podcast interview, Guardian US health reporter Jessica Glenza explains the practical implications of the status change for citizens. She discusses why the timing is particularly challenging for Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his Make America Healthy Again movement, and outlines the health priorities that newly elected Democrats are expected to pursue. The discussion is accompanied by clips from CBS, NBC, and CBC.
summary: The United States lost its measles elimination status, making the disease endemic after 26 years of elimination. Guardian health reporter Jessica Glenza says the change comes at a difficult time for health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr and his Make America Healthy Again movement, with newly elected Democrats set to focus on health.
author: Guardian Science

title: El Niño rains trigger record‑large flowering desert in Chile’s Atacama, 2026
content:
El Niño rains trigger an unprecedented “flowering desert” in Chile’s Atacama

An unusually wet winter in 2026 transformed parts of the Atacama Desert, one of the world’s driest regions, into a vivid landscape of red‑purple, green and white hues. The change followed a series of storm fronts that began in mid‑July, when an atmospheric river fed by a strengthening El Niño delivered one of the heaviest July rain events in decades across a stretch of Chile from the Atacama to Los Lagos, according to the Dirección Meteorológica de Chile. Back‑to‑back winter storms in August added rare snowfall to the desert floor.

Satellite imagery captured the progression of the bloom. On 14 September, the Operational Land Imager (OLI) on Landsat 8 recorded a section of the desert about 30 km southwest of Copiapó, revealing green areas capped with white that correspond to blooms of “suspiros” (Nolana), most likely Nolana baccata, as identified by Andres Moreira‑Muñoz of Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso. By 24 October, the OLI on Landsat 9 showed the same area dominated by red‑purple patches of “pata de guanaco” (Cistanthe), most likely Cistanthe longiscapa or another Cistanthe species, according to remote‑sensing scientist Roberto Chávez of the same university.

Chávez and colleagues photographed the Cistanthe blooms on the day the October image was acquired, using drones and digital cameras alongside the satellite data. Their project aims to map the spatial and temporal variation of the desert’s biodiversity to support land‑use planners and conservation managers. A second image pair, taken about 50 km southwest of Copiapó, highlights another priority area noted for its biological significance and flowering landscape.

The 2026 event stands out in the remote‑sensing record. A 2014 Landsat study mapped flowering and fog‑fed plants around the Copiapó dune field, and a 2019 analysis identified 13 desert blooms between 1981 and 2015. Moreira‑Muñoz described the 2026 bloom as “the most significant to date—in terms of its extent, intensity, and duration,” at least since the start of systematic remote‑sensing observations.

Images were provided by NASA’s Earth Observatory, photographed by Matías Pérez‑Evens and Roberto O. Chávez, and the accompanying story was written by Kathryn Hansen. The observations were part of Fondecyt Regular Project 1251184, a Chilean research initiative focused on the spatiotemporal variation of flowering desert biodiversity.
summary: Parts of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile turned red‑purple, green and white in austral spring 2026 after an unusually wet winter linked to a strengthening El Niño. Scientists say the bloom captured by Landsat images on September 14 and October 24 is the most extensive “desierto florido” observed by satellite remote sensing.
author: NASA News

title: APOD November 19, 2026 Shows Horsehead and Flame Nebulas
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 19, 2026 showcases a composite image of the Horsehead and Flame Nebulas. The accompanying explanation notes that the picture could be mistaken for a painting and describes the meaning of its colors. The brightest star visible to the left of the center is the blue Alnitak, identified as a triple‑star system and the easternmost star of Orion’s Belt.

At the image’s center the dark silhouette of the Horsehead Nebula is highlighted; it measures roughly five light‑years in height and lies about 1,500 light‑years from Earth. Dust and gas within the nebula block the red glow produced by hydrogen gas ionized by the nearby bright star Sigma Orionis, which appears at the top of the frame. To the left, the orange Flame Nebula is seen with dark filaments, while the nearby blue reflection nebula NGC 2023 is noted as actively forming stars.

The data for the image were gathered during almost six hours of observation at the Utah Desert Remote Observatories. The astrophotographer operated the equipment remotely from a home location in Illinois, more than 2,000 km away. Credit for the image goes to Mark E. Killion, and the entry lists Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell and Keighley Rockcliffe as authors and editors.
summary: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 19 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.
author: NASA News

title: Voyager 1 becomes first human-made object a light‑day from Earth
content: Voyager 1 stores its data on an eight‑track tape and has remained in communication with scientists for decades. It has now become the first human‑made object to reach a distance of one light‑day from Earth.
summary: Voyager 1 stores data on an eight‑track tape and has stayed in contact with scientists for decades. It is now the first human‑made object to travel a light‑day away from Earth.
author: Wired

title: ExpressVPN coupons provide up to 80% off subscription plans
content: ExpressVPN is promoting coupons that offer an 80% discount. The company also provides guidance on maximizing value from its subscription options, including a flexible one‑month plan and multi‑year deals that can deliver up to 61% savings.
summary: ExpressVPN coupons offer up to 80% off its subscription plans. The plans include a flexible 1‑month option and multi‑year deals that can lock in up to 61% savings.
author: Wired

title: Lawmakers seek new online‑harm protections and target Roblox arbitration before 2026
content:
Lawmakers are rushing to enact new protections for victims of online harm before the close of 2026, focusing on deep‑fake creators and platforms that prevent users from filing lawsuits.  

On Tuesday, a Senate Judiciary subcommittee held a hearing that called for ending forced‑arbitration clauses in online‑harassment cases. The hearing singled out Roblox, accusing the company of sidestepping legal complaints about alleged grooming of children by enforcing its own arbitration agreement on users who signed up as minors, including some as young as ten.
summary: Lawmakers are trying to pass protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, aimed at deepfake creators and platforms that block lawsuits. A Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing accused Roblox of using forced arbitration to limit legal complaints about alleged grooming of minors, including users under age ten.
author: The Verge

title: Elon Musk says Zelenskyy is lying about Starshield disruptions and misusing Starlink
content:
Elon Musk told attendees at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is “lying” about disruptions to Starshield in Ukraine and that Zelenskyy is attempting to misuse SpaceX’s consumer satellite‑internet service, Starlink, for military purposes. Musk said the remarks came as he tried to explain the ongoing dispute that has involved Zelenskyy, himself and the U.S. government over several weeks.  

Musk emphasized that Starlink was created as a civilian system and is not intended for “offensive drone strikes that kill people.” He added that any such capability would require Starshield, which he described as a separate, distinct system.
summary: Elon Musk says Zelenskyy is lying about Starshield disruptions and misusing Starlink.
author: The Verge

title: Will Wright announces MyMems, AI-driven simulation that mines player memories
content: The computer gaming world hasn't heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity, The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright's subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA. Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players' memories. MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright's previous projects by "turn[ing] the simulation inward," as Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning. The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world. “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?" Wright says by way of example in the release. "If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?" Read full article Comments
summary: Will Wright announces MyMems, AI-driven simulation that mines player memories.
author: Ars Technica

title: US loses measles elimination status as international health authorities announce
content: International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings. After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it " shameful " and a " national embarrassment." News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week. But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What's happening now is a runaway epidemic. Read full article Comments
summary: International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a designation achieved in 2000. The loss comes as measles cases have risen to over 5,400 this year, including more than 1,500 in Pennsylvania and 10 confirmed deaths across three states.
author: Ars Technica

title: Elon Musk says he isn’t MAGA and isn’t sure what the term means at NYT DealBook Summit
content: At the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Elon Musk said he was not sure what the term “MAGA” meant. He also remarked that he felt “pretty foolish” for having spent a large amount of money during the U.S. midterm elections.
summary: During his appearance Wednesday at The New York Times' DealBook Summit, Elon Musk said that he wasn't sure what the term "MAGA" meant and also commented that he felt "pretty foolish" for having spent so much money during the U. S.
author: TechCrunch

title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says AI prompted 60,000 employee buyout offers
content: In October, Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella said he offered buyouts to 60,000 employees, urging them to quit voluntarily rather than conducting another large‑scale layoff. He explained that the decision was driven by AI, though not in the manner most people might anticipate.
summary: Satya Nadella said he offered buyouts to 60,000 Microsoft employees in October, urging them to quit voluntarily rather than using a large layoff. He said the short answer is AI, but not in the way most people might expect.
author: TechCrunch

title: Critics call Grand Theft Auto VI a masterpiece after trailer hits 90 million views
content: Reviewers praise relationship between two leads in hotly anticipated release, whose trailer attracted 90m views in 24 hours Good things clearly come to those who wait. After 13 years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here – and, according to critics, it’s a masterpiece. The trailer for the video game, which returns players to Vice City, Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami, attracted more than 90m views in 24 hours when it was released in December 2023. Excitement continued to mount, with two release delays and a steady stream of leaks and speculation keeping the game in the headlines.
summary: Critics describe Grand Theft Auto VI as a masterpiece, praising the relationship between its two lead characters. Its trailer, released in December 2023, garnered more than 90 million views in 24 hours.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Grand Theft Auto seeded its own moral panic in 1997, experts say
content: Grand Theft Auto has been so central to the moral panic over graphic video games that some experts have called it the "grand theft fallacy". Yet the outrage was originally seeded by the studio itself in 1997 to drum up hype and taboo curiosity for its clunky-looking debut. Nearly 30 years on, that engineered scandal is still bearing fruit. Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love story
summary: Grand Theft Auto seeded its own moral panic in 1997, experts say.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Xi, Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen ahead of trilateral summit
content: On Thursday 19 November 2026, Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared together in Shenzhen, posing for a group photograph alongside other world leaders ahead of a closely watched trilateral summit.
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared together in Shenzhen on Thursday 19 November 2026. They posed for a group photograph with other world leaders ahead of a closely watched trilateral summit.
author: Euronews

title: Hundreds Celebrate Beaujolais Nouveau Arrival in Lyon with Night Parade
content: Lyon marked the arrival of Beaujolais Nouveau with a nighttime parade that featured wine barrels, flaming torches and brass music. Hundreds of participants gathered to celebrate and sample the first tastings of this year’s wine.
summary: Lyon welcomed the arrival of Beaujolais Nouveau with a nighttime parade featuring wine barrels, flaming torches and brass music. Hundreds gathered to celebrate the first tastings of the wine.
author: Euronews

title: Trump says US and China aim to help end Ukraine war at trilateral meeting with Russia
content: Ahead of a three‑president summit at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, President Trump said the United States and China want to help end the war in Ukraine. Analysts expect the trilateral meeting with Russia to be more symbolic than a source of concrete breakthroughs, and it comes as Russia’s offensive in Ukraine nears its five‑year anniversary. Trump met separately with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin before the summit.
summary: The three-president meeting will take place at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen. Analysts say the meeting will be more symbolic than yielding concrete breakthroughs, occurring as Russia's offensive in Ukraine approaches its five-year mark, after Trump met separately with Xi and Putin.
author: Euronews

title: European aerospace leaders urge EU‑UK security and defence partnership to work
content: Europe’s security environment will not wait for perfect alignment. Our leaders should seize the opportunities within reach. Our industry needs them to do so,' write Micael Johansson and David Lockwood, senior representatives of the European aerospace, security and defence industries, in an op-ed.
summary: Micael Johansson and David Lockwood, senior representatives of the European aerospace, security and defence industries, wrote an op‑ed calling for the EU‑UK Security and Defence Partnership to be made effective. They said Europe’s security environment will not wait for perfect alignment and that leaders should seize reachable opportunities for the industry.
author: Euronews

title: Kuo Zhang of Alibaba. Com says affordable AI tools give solo founders multinational power
content: European small businesses are described as ambitious and creative yet constrained by limited time and budgets. In an op‑ed for Euronews, Kuo Zhang of Alibaba.com argues that affordable, ready‑to‑use AI and global supply‑chain tools can provide solo founders with capabilities comparable to multinational firms, allowing them to concentrate on growth.
summary: European small businesses are ambitious and creative but lack time and budgets. In an Euronews op‑ed, Kuo Zhang of Alibaba. Com argues that affordable, ready‑to‑use AI and global supply‑chain tools give solo founders the capabilities of global companies, allowing them to focus on growth.
author: Euronews

title: Four killed, 13 injured in Russian strike on Odesa historic centre
content: Russian military strikes targeted the historic centre of Odesa, Ukraine, on Wednesday, 18 November 2026. The city’s military administration reported that the attack killed four people and injured at least 13 others.
summary: Russian strikes hit Odesa's historic centre, killing four people. At least 13 others were injured, the city’s military administration said.
author: Euronews

title: Ukraine drone and missile strike brings down part of Russia's Crimea bridge
content: A Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Monday night destroyed a section of the bridge that links the annexed Crimean Peninsula to Russia. The damage could cripple a route that Moscow has long used to move men and materiel into Crimea and the southern front. Kyiv continues to target the bridge because it has become a symbol of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s 2014 seizure of the peninsula.
summary: A Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Monday night brought down a stretch of the bridge linking the annexed Crimean Peninsula to Russia. The damage could cripple a route Moscow uses to move troops and equipment into Crimea and the southern front.
author: France 24

title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth visits Caracas, resumes military cooperation
content: U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announced a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and pledged to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip was the highest‑level U.S. visit since the ouster of Nicolás Maduro in January, marking a shift in bilateral relations.
summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and vowing to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip marks the highest-level US visit since the ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January, signalling a dramatic shift in relations between the two countries.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang did not accompany Trump to APEC after scandal
content: Jensen Huang, co‑founder of Nvidia, was originally slated to accompany the U.S. president to the APEC summit. However, the invitation was withdrawn after revelations surfaced that Huang had a personal relationship with a Chinese national. The timing of the scandal coincided with reports that a Singapore‑based client had used a backdoor method to evade sanctions on Nvidia’s powerful H200 chips. The incident has drawn attention to the complex interplay between U.S. technology firms and Chinese interests.
summary: Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang did not accompany Trump to APEC after scandal.
author: France 24

title: China, US and Russia leaders to hold first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting in Shenzhen
content: The leaders of China, the US and Russia are set to hold a first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting on Thursday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of an APEC summit. The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which Beijing said would involve "safeguarding world peace", has raised fears of a carve-up of the globe into "spheres of influence". Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will meet in Shenzhen on Thursday during the APEC summit. Beijing says the meeting aims to safeguard world peace, while observers fear it could divide the globe into spheres of influence.
author: France 24

title: Vanuatu's Environment Minister calls for UN climate summit reform ahead of COP31
content: Vanuatu’s Environment Minister Ralph Regenvanu urged reform of the United Nations climate‑summit process, saying a small group of countries is blocking progress. He cautioned that the upcoming COP31 could undo earlier climate commitments if the process is not changed.
summary: Vanuatu's Environment Minister Ralph Regenvanu said a small group of countries is blocking progress in the UN climate summit process. He warned that COP31 could reverse earlier commitments.
author: France 24

title: IEA says Middle East crisis is biggest threat to energy security in history
content: The International Energy Agency said on Thursday that the Middle East crisis sparked by U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in February represents the “largest threat” to energy security in history. The agency added that Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted oil shipments, causing consumers to shoulder a larger share of the costs.
summary: The International Energy Agency said the Middle East crisis triggered by US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February poses the largest threat to energy security in history. It warned that consumers were bearing more of the costs as Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted oil shipments.
author: France 24

title: FIFA 2026 rankings: France third, Morocco reaches fifth, highest for Africa
content: FIFA released its final world ranking for 2026, placing France in third position behind Spain and Argentina. The French team has now finished in the top three for the ninth consecutive year. Morocco moved up two places to fifth, matching the highest ranking ever attained by an African nation, a mark first set by Nigeria in 1994. Brazil fell to seventh, while Senegal is ranked 18th and Ivory Coast 28th.
summary: FIFA released its final 2026 world ranking, with France remaining third behind Spain and Argentina, marking its ninth consecutive year in the top three. Morocco rose two places to fifth, matching the best-ever ranking for an African nation, previously set by Nigeria in 1994.
author: France 24

title: Save the Children report: Nearly 1 in 4 children live in conflict zones
content: A new Save the Children report finds that almost one‑in‑four children are living in conflict zones. The report also notes that violations against children—including denial of humanitarian access, abductions and sexual violence—have risen dramatically over the past year.
summary: A new Save the Children report finds that almost one in four children worldwide now live in conflict zones. The report also says that denial of humanitarian access, abductions and sexual violence against children have increased dramatically over the past year.
author: DW World

title: MAIB report says Mike Lynch’s yacht Bayesian had unknown high‑wind vulnerability
content:
The UK Marine Accident Investigations Branch report says the 56‑metre superyacht Bayesian was vulnerable to knockdown in high winds, a weakness that had not been identified because the vessel had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down.

Anchored near the fishing port of Porticello, the yacht sank during a violent storm shortly before dawn on 19 August 2024, killing seven people, including tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter.
summary: MAIB report says Mike Lynch’s yacht Bayesian had unknown high‑wind vulnerability.
author: Guardian World

title: General Pants Co enters voluntary administration, risking nearly 500 jobs
content:
General Pants Co, an Australian youth‑fashion chain, has entered voluntary administration, placing nearly 500 jobs at risk. The move marks the latest instance of a major retailer seeking administration as Australia’s retail sector grapples with cash‑strapped shoppers and competition from online‑only operators.  

The development follows the recent collapses of upmarket department store David Jones and premium womenswear brands Cue and Veronika Maine, highlighting the pressure on established retailers amid tough economic conditions.
summary: General Pants Co has entered voluntary administration, putting nearly 500 jobs at risk. The collapse follows recent failures of David Jones, Cue and Veronika Maine, highlighting pressure on Australian retailers.
author: Guardian World

title: Wreck of Australia's first locally built warship HMCS Spitfire found off north Queensland
content: HMCS Spitfire was commissioned by colonial government to protect against Russian warships during the Crimean war The wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship has been discovered 128 years after sinking off the coast of far north Queensland. Marine archaeologists found the remains of Ex HMCS Spitfire on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898.
summary: The wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship, Ex HMCS Spitfire, was discovered off the coast of far north Queensland. Marine archaeologists located the remains on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898, 128 years later.
author: Guardian World

title: NSW inquest finds mother chose home birth for twins despite expert advice
content: Inquest into deaths of four babies in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 told mother refused to give birth in hospital after hearing others’ traumatic stories Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Baby B’s mother was so determined to have a home birth she ignored the advice of experts – including her own midwife, an inquest has heard. The inquest heard she was pregnant with twins, which she described as a “wonderful shock”, and didn’t want a hospital birth because she had heard of others’ traumatic experiences.
summary: NSW inquest finds mother chose home birth for twins despite expert advice.
author: Guardian World

title: Coroner says Aboriginal inmate Tammy Shipley's death after drinking 20L water was preventable
content:
A coroner’s inquest has concluded that the death of Tammy Michelle Shipley, a 47‑year‑old Aboriginal woman, was preventable. Shipley collapsed after drinking at least 20 litres of water while in a cell at Silverwater women’s correctional centre in New South Wales, and died on 20 December 2022.

The inquest found that required regular monitoring of Shipley was not carried out, and that “excess consumption of water” could have been prevented if checks had been performed as required. The coroner described the outcome as the result of systemic failures within the prison.
summary: Tammy Michelle Shipley, a 47‑year‑old Aboriginal woman, died at Silverwater women’s correctional centre on 20 December 2022 after collapsing from drinking at least 20 litres of water. A coroner’s inquest concluded the death was preventable and resulted from systemic failures to monitor her as required.
author: Guardian World

title: IEA warns datacentres will emit 70% more carbon by 2030 as AI demand soars
content:
The International Energy Agency (IEA), the world’s energy watchdog, warns that datacentres will create 70 % more carbon emissions by 2030 as the United States and China turn to fossil fuels to power their artificial‑intelligence growth agendas.

The IEA also forecasts that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three‑quarters of this growth.
summary: The International Energy Agency says global datacentres will emit 70% more carbon by 2030. It warns that datacentres will use twice as much electricity by 2030, with AI expansion—driven by the United States and China’s reliance on fossil fuels—accounting for three‑quarters of the increase.
author: Guardian World

title: UN report finds one in four women worldwide cannot refuse sex in marriage
content:
A UN report released on Thursday found that one in four women worldwide lack the power to refuse sex when their husband or partner demands it. The study, issued by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA), highlights regional variations in this lack of consent.

In West and Central Africa, 45 % of women reported they cannot say no to sex within their own marriage. In East and Southern Africa and in Arab states, a third (33 %) face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, the figure is lower, with one in ten women unable to refuse sex.
summary: A UN Population Fund report says one in four women globally lack the power to refuse sex when a husband or partner demands it. The study reports 45% of women in west and central Africa, 33% in east and southern Africa and Arab states, and 10% in Latin America and the Caribbean cannot say no.

title: Ireland's Prendergast cleared to face South Africa after hip-drop tackle ban dismissed
content:
Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will face South Africa in the Nations Championship on Saturday after an independent disciplinary committee dismissed his citation for an alleged hip-drop tackle. The 23-year-old was originally cited for a challenge on Fiji captain Peceli Yato, an offense under Law 9.13 introduced in November. Following a hearing on Tuesday, the committee decided no further action would be taken, sparing Prendergast a potential suspension.

South Africa Rugby also condemned online abuse directed at officials, while coach Rassie Erasmus had previously predicted the player would be cleared.
summary: Ireland's fly-half Sam Prendergast is available to face South Africa in the Nations Championship after an independent disciplinary committee dismissed his citation for an alleged hip-drop tackle. The 23-year-old was cited for a challenge against Fiji's captain Peceli Yato, but the committee decided no further action would be taken.
author: Guardian Sport

title: MLB Commissioner Manfred Says Owners Will Not Budge on Salary Cap, Lockout Looms
content: 2027 season under threat amid dispute over salary cap Commissioner says fans want a more equal game MLB commissioner, Rob Manfred, has insisted owners will not budge from their demand for a salary cap, leaving the league on track for a lockout starting 2 December that could threaten the 2027 season. “I can’t imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor,” Manfred said on Wednesday at a news conference during an owners meeting. Players say they will never accept a cap. The last time management proposed a cap in 1994, it led to a strike that lasted almost eight months and caused the cancellation of the World Series for the first time in 90 years.
summary: MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred stated that owners will not accept a deal without a salary cap and floor, putting the league on track for a lockout starting December 2. Players have rejected the cap concept, and the dispute threatens the 2027 season amid a history of labor conflicts.

title: Emma Hayes to assist US Soccer in search for next USMNT coach
content:
US women’s national team head coach Emma Hayes has confirmed her participation in the search for the next USMNT manager. Speaking after announcing her squad for the Concacaf championship and World Cup qualifier, Hayes stated she is confident in the group assembled to select Mauricio Pochettino’s replacement. Pochettino recently departed for Manchester United.

The selection committee includes Hayes, US Soccer CEO JT Batson, chief operating officer Dan Helfrich, and vice-president of sporting Oguchi Onyewu. Hayes, who won the 2024 Olympics and enjoyed a trophy-laden tenure at Chelsea, shed light on her role in this hiring process for the first time.
summary: US women’s national team head coach Emma Hayes said she is confident in the group selected to find a replacement for Mauricio Pochettino. The search team includes US Soccer CEO JT Batson, chief operating officer Dan Helfrich, and vice-president of sporting Oguchi Onyewu.

title: Leicester City ends BC Game sponsorship after porn actor partnership
content:
Leicester City has terminated its front-of-shirt sponsorship agreement with BC Game, an offshore cryptocurrency casino registered in Belize that is unlicensed to operate in the UK. The club, which had partnered with the betting firm since 2024, cited “differing commercial priorities” as the reason for prematurely ending the deal on Wednesday.

The decision followed a fan backlash triggered when BC Game named Eva Elfie, a porn actor, as a brand ambassador this month. In response to the partnership, the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, highlighted the “devastating impacts” associated with gambling and pornography.
summary: Leicester City terminated its front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with cryptocurrency casino BC Game following a fan backlash over the company's partnership with Eva Elfie. The club cited differing commercial priorities for the early end to the agreement, which had been in place since 2024.

title: Veerle Buurman scores late winner as Chelsea beat PSG in WCL
content:
Veerle Buurman scored a late winner to help Chelsea edge past Paris Saint-Germain in a Champions League match. The goal secured three points for Chelsea, who struggled to break down a resilient PSG defense. The victory temporarily placed Chelsea at the top of the league phase table.

Buurman continued her strong form following a standout performance against Manchester City earlier that weekend, where she came on as a substitute and was named player of the match. In the match against PSG, she was the decisive factor, finding the net at the near post after Chelsea created numerous chances without scoring.
summary: Veerle Buurman scored a late goal to help Chelsea defeat Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. The victory temporarily places Chelsea at the top of the league phase table.

title: Rugby brain injury lawsuits at collapse risk after document disclosure delays
content:
Rugby brain injury lawsuits involving hundreds of players are nearing collapse due to repeated delays in disclosing medical documents. Lead counsel Paul Downes KC conceded in June that the claimants were in the “last-chance saloon” after missing court-mandated deadlines, a situation that has worsened following another failure to meet requirements in October. The legal team is now arguing for an extension until January to prevent the cases from failing.

The future of these six-year-old, high-cost legal battles rests on upcoming decisions by two judges. The claimants’ consistent failure to disclose documents to the defendants has placed the proceedings on the brink of termination, with the current status described as being beyond the previous “last-chance” warning.
summary: The lead counsel for the claimants has conceded that the lawsuits are in the "last-chance saloon" after repeatedly missing court-mandated deadlines for document disclosure. The future of the case now rests on the decisions of two judges following the claimants' failure to meet a deadline in October.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United's 1974 relegation offers warning for current decline
content:
Manchester United’s current relegation zone position, its first in 40 years, draws striking parallels to the club’s 1974 relegation. The article highlights similarities in both eras, including the departure of a legendary manager whose shadow remained, alongside boardroom uncertainty and the rapid turnover of replacements.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side but stayed on as a director. This mirrors the situation with Sir Alex Ferguson, who watched from the Old Trafford directors’ box as his successors tried and failed, leading to the club’s slide over several years.
summary: The article highlights striking parallels between Manchester United's 1974 relegation and the club's current presence in the relegation zone for the first time in 40 years. It notes that in both eras, a legendary manager departed while remaining a director, leading to boardroom uncertainty and a succession of failed replacements.

title: Cameron Bancroft exposes details of 2018 Australian cricket cheating scandal
content: The time for formal measures has passed but all involved have betrayed the trust of a country whose Test team is sacred Cry havoc. But Cameron Bancroft did not let anything slip, not after close to a decade of keeping his mouth firmly shut. It was a deliberate, considered and lengthy deed of revelation that the former Test opening bat chose to publish in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday, claiming to finally fill in a wealth of detail around Australian cricket’s 2018 cheating scandal that so many others seem to have gone to such lengths to keep concealed. It was also a devastating repudiation of Pat Cummins, a teammate of equivalent juniority to Bancroft during their few months playing together, but now the Test captain, who had delivered his own manifesto in spoken form at a press conference last week. That version of events, in which Cummins was adamant that he had never been aware of any kind of ball-tampering in Australian colours, was what pushed Bancroft from silence to speech. “It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone,” Bancroft wrote. “What I saw, experienced and lived with not only him, but everyone else on that tour in South Africa is not the public account he gave in his press conference and in the years previously.”
summary: Former Test opening bat Cameron Bancroft published a detailed account of the 2018 Australian cricket cheating scandal in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday. His revelations repudiated Test captain Pat Cummins, who had denied any knowledge of ball‑tampering during a press conference last week.

title: Researchers warn most children labeled allergic to antibiotics may not be allergic
content:
Researchers caution that most children identified as allergic to antibiotics may not actually have an allergy.  

At 7 p.m. on a Saturday, a 10‑year‑old boy with severe tonsillitis arrived at an urgent‑care center. Clinician Rebecca Payne asked his mother, “Does he have any allergies?” before choosing an appropriate antibiotic.
summary: Researchers warn that most children labeled as allergic to antibiotics may not actually have an allergy. In an urgent care visit, a 10-year-old boy with severe tonsillitis was asked by Rebecca Payne about any antibiotic allergies.

title: Doctors warn NHS AI recruitment platform could miss top talent
content: Doctors warn that the use of AI in medical recruitment could result in missing top talent. This concern arises as NHS England prepares to implement a £1.2 billion AI-driven workforce management and recruitment platform. A new report from BMJ Careers highlights issues regarding quality, fairness, and the handling of a surge in AI-powered applications by medical recruiters.
summary: A new report from BMJ Careers raises concerns about quality and fairness as NHS England prepares to introduce a £1.2 billion AI-driven workforce management platform. Medical recruiters are responding to a flood of AI-powered applications, prompting warnings that the system may overlook top talent.

title: Norwegian trial finds no clear benefit from two drugs for spontaneous birth after induction
content: A large Norwegian trial published in The BMJ reports that there is no clear evidence that hyoscine butylbromide or sodium bicarbonate improves spontaneous vaginal birth rates in first-time mothers after labor induction. The study specifically examined spontaneous births without the assistance of forceps or vacuum. While the researchers note that small benefits of either drug cannot be entirely ruled out, they conclude that the findings do not support the routine use of these medications.
summary: A large Norwegian trial published by The BMJ found no clear evidence that hyoscine butylbromide or sodium bicarbonate improves spontaneous vaginal birth rates in first-time mothers after labor induction. Researchers concluded that the findings do not support the routine use of these drugs, although small benefits cannot be entirely ruled out.

content: An experimental drug for a rare and aggressive form of ALS may soon become available to patients. This treatment developed from basic and clinical research conducted at Columbia University's Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons.

content: A new study led by experts at the University of Nottingham offers new insight into the performance of a commonly used colorectal cancer test in individuals under 50. title: Study: Extensive management of calcareous grasslands protects wild bee diversity in Europe
content:
Calcareous grasslands, rare wildflower-rich ecosystems found on shallow, alkaline soils over chalk or limestone bedrock, serve as critical habitats for wild bees and other pollinators. An international research team led by the University of Göttingen investigated how management practices affect these valuable communities. The study revealed that both long-term abandonment and intensive management threaten wild bee diversity in these areas.

The researchers concluded that extensive management of calcareous grasslands, combined with appropriate nature conservation measures in the surrounding landscape, is crucial for protecting these habitats. These findings have been published in the Journal of Applied Ecology, highlighting the importance of connected habitats and specific management strategies for maintaining pollinator diversity in Europe.
summary: An international team led by the University of Göttingen found that long-term abandonment or intensive management threatens wild bee diversity in calcareous grasslands. The study, published in the Journal of Applied Ecology, states that extensive management and surrounding conservation measures are crucial for supporting these habitats.

title: Webb confirms first merger of supergiant and sun-like star in Andromeda
content: Researchers recently identified a first of its kind: A star slightly less massive than the sun spiraled into and merged with a puffy supergiant star on the outskirts of our neighboring Andromeda galaxy. They nicknamed the newly single, potentially "rejuvenated" star Bao. Their discovery was then bolstered by quick-turn observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope that were carefully cross-referenced with extensive data from telescopes in space and on the ground.
summary: Researchers identified a star slightly less massive than the sun that merged with a supergiant star in the Andromeda galaxy. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observations confirmed the discovery of the resulting single star, nicknamed Bao.
author: Phys.org

title: AI models show gender bias in resume writing and hiring assessments
content:
Artificial intelligence systems may introduce gender bias into the hiring process by embedding stereotypes into resume creation and evaluation. When a woman uses AI to draft her resume, the system selects specific words and highlights certain qualities to build her professional profile. If a subsequent system, potentially based on the same underlying model, evaluates that text, it may reinforce these initial biases.

This scenario creates a “double filter” where gender stereotypes enter the application stage and are further amplified during the selection process. The result is that bias is not only present in the candidate’s materials but is also reinforced by the automated assessment tools used to review them.
summary: AI systems may introduce gender stereotypes when generating resume content, creating a potential double filter in the hiring process. This bias is further reinforced when similar models evaluate the generated text.
author: Phys.org

title: Temperature fingerprints reveal electrocatalytic reaction rates and activation enthalpy
content:
Electrocatalysis is essential for converting renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals, with industrial electrolyzers generally operating at moderately elevated temperatures. Measuring how reaction rates vary with temperature provides a powerful, though underexplored, method for determining the factors that control these reactions.

These temperature-based measurements yield two specific quantities: an apparent activation enthalpy, which reflects the energetic cost of the reaction, and a prefactor linked to the activation entropy.
summary: Measuring how electrocatalytic reaction rates change with temperature provides a method to probe reaction controls. These measurements yield an apparent activation enthalpy and a prefactor linked to activation entropy.
author: Phys.org

title: Q&A: Schools that ban cellphones see uptick in test scores
content: As the smartphone era approaches two milestones, January will mark 20 years since Steve Jobs first unveiled the iPhone from a stage in San Francisco.

title: Natural History Museum displays striking beetles from Maxwell Barclay's "Interesting Beetles"
content:
Maxwell Barclay, senior curator in charge of beetles at the Natural History Museum in London, highlights the diversity and significance of beetles in his book, Interesting Beetles. He notes that beetles are older than dinosaurs and account for nearly a quarter of all species on Earth. Barclay observes that except for Antarctica, one is never more than a few meters from a beetle anywhere on the land surface. The book showcases specimens from the museum’s archives, emphasizing that with 400,000 species, each has a unique story to tell.

The text details several specific species that demonstrate the insect’s adaptability. The glorious flower chafer (Howdenypa gloriosa) features opalescent green and blue coloring and flies with its wing cases closed, a maneuver that has attracted the interest of aerospace engineers who have fitted some chafers with tiny wireless transmitters to study their flight. In contrast, the Colorado potato beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata) is described as a worldwide pest that developed a destructive relationship with humans after the potato was introduced to North America.

Other featured insects include the carbuncle frog-legged beetle (Sagra carbunculus), which uses its buff hind legs for battle and mating competition, and the violin beetle (Mormolyce phyllodes), which blends in with fallen leaves in tropical rainforests despite being an inelegant flyer. The desert fog-basking beetle (Onymacris bicolor) is noted for its ability to survive in arid environments like the Namib desert by climbing dunes to collect dew from special structures on its wings.

Barclay concludes that beetles are integral parts of their respective ecosystems, ranging from potato fields to deserts. He writes that without beetles serving as predators, pollinators, herbivores, or scavengers, many ecosystems would be unable to function.
summary: The glorious flower chafer Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum What animal is older than the dinosaurs and accounts for nearly a quarter of species on Earth? It is the magnificent beetle, an insect whose wings rest underneath a hard, protective case that often displays beautiful colours and intricate ornaments.
author: New Scientist

title: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
content:
MIT researchers have found that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age. This decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.

Surprisingly, some older adults retain the same powerful cleansing waves seen in younger people.
summary: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age. The decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.
author: Science Daily

title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s
content: Scientists have identified the protein SORLA as a natural defense against Alzheimer’s disease. In mouse studies, boosting SORLA levels significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected neural connections, and prevented some brain shrinkage. Conversely, removing the protein worsened the damage, underscoring its critical protective role and potential for new treatments.
summary: Scientists have uncovered a powerful natural defense against Alzheimer’s disease that could open the door to new treatments. By boosting a protein called SORLA, researchers significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected connections between brain cells, and prevented some of the brain shrinkage associated with neurodegeneration in mice.
author: Science Daily

title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
content: A 125,000-year-old discovery in Saudi Arabia indicates that hippos and other wildlife inhabited the region when it featured enormous lakes rather than the current vast desert. The site yielded thousands of stone tools and ancient plant remains, which suggest early humans thrived there and utilized sophisticated hunting techniques, potentially involving weapons enhanced with poisonous plant compounds.
summary: A remarkable 125,000-year-old discovery in Saudi Arabia reveals that early humans once thrived beside enormous lakes filled with wildlife in what is now a vast desert. Thousands of stone tools and ancient plant remains suggest these prehistoric people used sophisticated hunting techniques, potentially including weapons enhanced with poisonous plant compounds.

title: Senate committee rejects Trump nominee to lead National Science Foundation
content:
Senate committee chair Bill Cassidy, a Republican from Louisiana, announced that Jim O’Neill will not undergo a confirmation hearing to lead the National Science Foundation. Cassidy, who heads the Senate committee on health, education, labor, and pensions, stated that O’Neill “did not do enough to stand up for science” in his previous position. This decision effectively ends O’Neill’s run for the top US scientific organization.

The NSF is described as an embattled independent federal agency that has experienced major budget cuts and grant freezes under the Trump administration. The article notes that the next nominee for the NSF position will face a Democratic-led Senate.
summary: Senate committee rejects Trump nominee to lead National Science Foundation.

title: Colibactin from E. coli Toxin Suspected in Rising Early‑Onset Bowel Cancer
content:
Scientists have told the House of Commons that exposure to colibactin, a bacterial toxin produced by E. coli, is a leading suspect in the rising rates of bowel cancer among individuals under 50. They identified early-life exposure to this toxin as a potential driver of early-onset colorectal cancer.

Cases of early-onset bowel cancer have doubled in many countries over the past two decades. While researchers acknowledge that rising obesity and a decline in physical activity contribute to this trend, they believe other factors must also be involved to explain the increase.
summary: Scientists told MPs that exposure to colibactin in early life may drive early‑onset colorectal cancer. Cases of early‑onset bowel cancer have doubled in many countries in the past two decades, and researchers say obesity and reduced physical activity are contributors but other factors are likely involved.
