title: MAF EAP Offers Holiday Stress Management Tips
content: 6 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Feet in woolen socks by the fireplace. Holidays are often a fun break during a busy year – a long weekend here and there is an event many of us can get behind. However, when a short holiday break turns into a full holiday season, we know that this is a different “ball game”. Everyone has stress about something – some people love the holidays, and some people are holiday-avoidant… and some live in the middle. What specific stressors or challenges you experience might not bother your sibling, your spouse or your coworker. We want to be aware of and have a clear understanding of what holidays mean to you as a person. The first step is to acknowledge what your feelings and emotions are – you may enjoy seeing the neighborhood holiday lights but not want to decorate yourself (totally okay!!), you may love shopping for the perfect gift for everyone on your list, you may avoid all of the activities — everyone one of these is an okay choice… you can be yourself always in all ways. Give yourself that permission. As you prepare, keep a list or a calendar of events – expected/obligated, okay to go or not go, Holiday Calendar: Expected/ Obligated Need to do Would be fun to do Nope Family dinner Work party off-site Travel Host at my house Religious services Neighborhood party Shopping Restaurants Combine this with your standard calendar and make a schedule. If you want, add to the list what your part is (bring a dish, gift, coordinate a visit, etc.). Having the majority of activities written down will help you not overbook, help you plan ahead, make it easier to say no, spend within your budget. Before you commit to something, say “I have to check my calendar first…. I will get back to you”. Prepare your budget – We often budget for gifts but forget that we will be buying more groceries for those special meals and favorite dishes…. We also need to budget for travel, having guests in your home, clothing, even allow for a higher electric bill. Write it down – keep receipts – let your immediate family know that this is what we have to spend, then track it as you go. Now that you have a current calendar and a working budget, set realistic expectations for your holiday experience. We know that not everything is optional and traditions will continue but none of it has to be perfect…minor stress and family friction can be normal. When telling someone no, use “I” statements and stick to the single issue at hand. In addition to your list/calendar, remember to prioritize time for yourself. Keep your regular sleep schedule as much as possible, eat well (if you have a heavy meal one day, lighten up the next), schedule time to get fresh air and a quick break. ALWAYS focus on what matters. Focus on meaningful connections rather than activities that cause you anxiety. If you feel emotional, take a few moments alone and identify the feeling, honor yourself for being able to face it and breathe through it (avoid pushing it down). Remember how many times you have gotten through a “pressure moment” and give yourself credit. Call a trusted friend or your therapist if you feel overwhelmed for longer than a day…. And, please call 988 if you feel overwhelmed to an extreme. 988 is always available and waiting to help. Look for the glimmers – find a happy moment (no matter how brief), find the memories that make you smile. Thinking of something joyful changes your emotional state… train yourself to do this any time you need a lift. Ultimately, we want to move away from focusing on the future (It causes anxiety) or overthinking about the past (it causes depression) …. And find yourself in the here and now where you have power to manage things happening around you. Your power is with you in the present. (Eckert Tolle book – The Power of Now). The holiday season lasts for weeks – gift yourself with Honoring yourself – take a break if you need to Asking for help when necessary Preparing well and being realistic Acknowledge your emotions (holidays can be sad as well as joyful) Respect differences – focus on the reason you are together and celebrating Make adjustments as you go Give yourself Grace and Space Person sitting on sofa next to a holiday tree. With the extra pressure of the holiday season, our feelings can often be stronger than other times during the year…. If you start having feelings: Anxious – take deep breaths, focus ONLY on the present – your surroundings, what you see, count objects, put ice on the inside of your wrists (this works really well!) Angry – walk away for a moment, take a break, give yourself as long as you need to regulate these feelings, know that whoever gets angry first loses…be the winner in the moment. Helpless, hopeless, trapped (discouraged) – remember that you have a voice, it is sometimes difficult to use it in family situations, but you can talk to yourself. Remember how strong you are, how many accomplishments you have completed…. Reframe the situation so you recall all of your wonderful qualities. Overwhelmed – Check your list/holiday calendar again…what can you change or take off the list. What can you postpone for 24-48 hours? What can you give someone else to do? What can you order from the store rather than do the cooking or shopping yourself? Find a quick solution for one or two things (at least) and take some pressure off. Grief – acknowledge how you feel, we do not have to be cheerful just because it is a holiday. Say no to any event or activity that feels too “heavy” and give yourself permission to leave if it becomes too much. Find a way to keep their memory with you – carry a favorite picture or memento. Find a grief support group. Basically, we want to notice the small things and find gratitude in what we have. Our outward situation does not define us. If you find that holiday time is difficult or stressful, always give yourself permission to contact your EAP services for assistance and support.
summary: MAF EAP advises employees to manage holiday stress by creating a calendar of obligations and setting realistic budgets. The guidance encourages prioritizing self-care, using "I" statements to set boundaries, and contacting EAP services or the 988 hotline for support.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Sets Nov. 29 Launch for Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission to ISS
content:
NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX have targeted a launch window beginning no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST on Sunday, Nov. 29, for the Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission. The spacecraft, a Cygnus XL, will ride atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The mission is designed to deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station.

Pre-launch activities include a media teleconference scheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, at 12 p.m. The call will feature Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager for NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program; Jennifer Buchli, chief scientist for the same program; Dave Schiller, vice president of civil space and sciences at Northrop Grumman; and Jared Metter, director of flight reliability at SpaceX. Media participants must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom by 11 a.m. on Nov. 23 to obtain call details and must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the teleconference.

Upon arrival at the International Space Station on Tuesday, Dec. 1, NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will utilize the Canadarm2 robotic arm to capture the Cygnus XL at 2:35 a.m. Ground controllers will subsequently install the spacecraft on the Unity module’s Earth-facing port to facilitate cargo unloading. The spacecraft is named the S. S. James “Jim” A. Lovell in honor of the former NASA astronaut, who flew on four missions including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and Apollo 13.

The cargo includes research aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis, predicting cancer spread, and advancing treatments for muscle loss. Additional experiments focus on improving radiation sensing and advancing food production for future long-duration missions. The spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the orbiting laboratory until May 2027, at which point it will depart with several thousand pounds of disposal items and other unneeded cargo, burning up harmlessly during re-entry.

NASA will provide live coverage of the launch and docking events through various platforms, with launch coverage beginning at 10:25 a.m. on Nov. 29. On-demand streaming video and photos will be available shortly after liftoff. Members of the public can register to attend the launch virtually through NASA’s virtual guest program, which includes curated resources and a digital passport stamp. Additional updates will be posted on NASA’s space station blog, and the agency encourages engagement on social media by tagging specific NASA and ISS accounts on X, Facebook, and Instagram.
summary: NASA Sets Nov. 29 Launch for Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission to ISS.
author: NASA News

title: Mastra Factory: Open-source agentic tool merges 238 PRs weekly for Mastra
content:
Shane, Sam, and Abhi have introduced Mastra Factory, an open-source software factory designed to assist in maintaining the Mastra TypeScript agent framework. The team notes that Mastra has grown significantly since its initial launch nearly two years ago, now averaging nearly four million downloads per week. To manage this scale, the team utilizes Factory to merge hundreds of pull requests weekly across the mastra-ai GitHub organization. In the week prior to the announcement, Factory opened and merged 238 pull requests, complementing 630 merged pull requests created by human developers.

The authors define Factory as a configurable agentic kanban board that can be tagged in Slack. Its architecture relies on Mastra’s durable agents for long-running sessions, a conversational memory system, and a markdown-based wiki with source citations for company knowledge. The system also incorporates signals that subscribe to PR comments and utilizes a customizable cloud sandbox with a coding harness currently being adapted to support tools like Claude Code and Codex.

Initially modeled around a workflow-oriented process of triage, plan, build, review, and shipped, the team has shifted to primarily driving the tool through Slack rather than a web interface. Senior engineers now use the platform to run parallel sessions, such as triaging older issues. Additionally, the team has integrated bug and vulnerability scanners and closed the repository to outside contributors, requesting detailed issue reproductions instead. Mastra Factory is fully open-source, allowing users to run it on their own infrastructure via `npm create factory`, though a hosted version is also available.
summary: Mastra Factory is an open-source software factory that uses durable agents and a configurable kanban board to maintain the Mastra framework. The tool recently opened and merged 238 pull requests in a week, alongside 630 merged by humans.
author: Hacker News

title: CreditNirvana vulnerabilities exposed 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings
content: Vulnerabilities in the CreditNirvana AI debt collection platform exposed 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings. The security flaws would have allowed attackers to access sensitive data, including emails, texts, and credit reports.
summary: Serious vulnerabilities in the CreditNirvana platform would have allowed attackers to access detailed sensitive information. The exposed data included emails, texts, credit reports, and 315,000 call recordings.
author: Wired

title: Instagram allows editing Stories for 15 minutes without losing engagement
content:
Instagram has introduced a new feature allowing users to edit their Stories after posting without losing views, likes, or replies. Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced that users can now modify text, music, stickers, and drawings for up to 15 minutes after sharing. This update eliminates the previous requirement to delete and repost a Story to fix errors or add forgotten elements.

The feature was first spotted by reverse engineer Alessandro Paluzzi in April, but it is now officially available. To use the tool, users can open their Story and select the three-dot menu located in the bottom-right corner.
summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced that users can now edit text, music, stickers, and drawings in their Stories for up to 15 minutes after posting. This update eliminates the need to delete and repost Stories to fix errors, as views, likes, and replies are preserved during edits.
author: The Verge

title: Sony’s impressive Bravia 8 II OLED hits a new low price ahead of Black Friday
content:
The 65-inch Sony Bravia 8 II OLED television is currently available for under $2,200, representing a $1,100 discount from its typical price. This price point, described as the lowest observed, is offered by retailers including Amazon, Best Buy, and Sony directly. The deal is positioned as an early alternative to waiting for Black Friday sales. Additionally, the 55-inch model is discounted by $800, reducing its cost from the standard $2,599.99 to just under $1,800 at the same retail locations.

The Bravia 8 II was selected as the “king of TV” by a panel of judges, which included The Verge’s Nilay Patel, during Value Electronics’ 2025 shootout. The television features excellent color accuracy, a bright panel, and a 120Hz refresh rate. Its image quality is attributed to impressive image processing and bold colors produced by a quantum dot-equipped OLED panel. The screen is noted for looking good out of the box, though reviewers recommend using Professional mode.

For gaming, the panel supports up to 120Hz at 4K resolution, incorporating variable refresh rate and automatic low-latency mode. Connectivity options include two HDMI 2.1 ports, one of which supports eARC, along with two HDMI 2.0 ports. The Verge’s John Higgins praised the TV’s image quality and engaging picture, noting that while these traits are common among OLEDs, the Bravia 8 II distinguishes itself through its processing and color output. The review also noted some color fringing in dark scenes but still recommended the screen.
summary: The Bravia 8 II has deep and inky blacks, giving great depth to space images. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Black Friday is a great time to save on a new OLED television for your winter movie nights.
author: The Verge

title: Nvidia Generates $8,300 in Pure Profit Every Second
content:
Nvidia’s latest earnings data highlight a staggering level of profitability. According to the report, the company generates roughly $8,300 in pure profit every second. By the time a reader finishes the paragraph, Nvidia would have accumulated about $45,000 in profit.

The article notes that Nvidia’s founder and former CEO has recently stepped down amid a series of scandals. Despite this leadership change, the company is portrayed as far from a typical “semi‑successful” firm that might need a new CEO to correct course. Instead, it is described as an exceptionally successful enterprise that continues to perform strongly in its core markets.
summary: Nvidia now makes $8,300 in pure profit each second. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change.
author: The Verge

title: Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
content:
President Donald Trump arrived at Manila’s Villamor Air Base on November 17, 2026, where he was welcomed by a group of five beauty queens, according to local news outlet Rappler. As he stepped onto the tarmac, a child handed him small United States and Philippine flags. A band performed “YMCA,” a song frequently used at Trump rallies, while additional girls in traditional bell‑sleeved blouses and young men in wide‑brimmed hats danced to the tune.

Outside the airport, hundreds of protesters filled the streets, carrying signs and at least one prop casket that read “Trump out.” Other demonstrators displayed signs reading “Reject Pax Silica,” referencing the U.S.-led international initiative aimed at securing chips and critical minerals. The event, captured in a Getty Images photo, highlighted both the ceremonial reception and the public opposition surrounding Trump’s visit.
summary: Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines.
author: The Verge

title: James Gunn and Peter Safran Exit DC Studios After Skydance Acquisition
content:
James Gunn and Peter Safran have stepped down as co‑heads of DC Studios after Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Their departure leaves the future of the cinematic universe that had been developing around films such as last year’s Superman uncertain. While Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow feature may still be released, his broader plans for the DC Universe appear to be at risk under the new leadership.

The studio’s newly appointed CEO, Jeremy Latcham, has reportedly been given a mandate by Skydance CEO David Ellison to fast‑track certain projects. Gunn had been slowly building the DCU with less high‑profile characters such as Peacemaker, Supergirl, and Clayface, but Latcham’s directive suggests a shift toward accelerating the studio’s output.
summary: James Gunn and Peter Safran have left their positions as co‑heads of DC Studios after Skydance acquired Warner Bros. Discovery. The new CEO, Jeremy Latcham, has been given a mandate by Skydance CEO David Ellison to fast‑track the DC Universe, potentially altering Gunn's original plans.
author: The Verge

title: Cruz starts FCC confirmation hearing with Democrats absent
content:
Senate Commerce Committee Chair Ted Cruz (R-TX) initiated a Wednesday meeting to confirm President Donald Trump’s nominee, Brendan Carr, to the Federal Communications Commission. The session featured a lopsided dais, with all 14 Republican members present, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD), while roughly a dozen empty chairs indicated the absence of every Democratic panel member. Cruz stated he learned the previous night that Democrats intended to boycott the vote.

Democrats, however, contend they had repeatedly raised concerns about advancing a Republican FCC nominee without a Democratic counterpart. The article notes that Cruz began to explain the administration's willingness in this context, though the specific details of his statement are cut off in the provided text.
summary: Cruz starts FCC confirmation hearing with Democrats absent.
author: The Verge

title: Largest U.S. school districts consider ditching Google Search
content:
New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago school districts are evaluating alternatives to Google Search after the company announced it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features. According to The New York Times, beginning next year schools will not be able to turn off Gemini‑powered features without also disabling Search. Google’s vice president of education, Chris Phillips, explained that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools disabling AI features “will not have access to Search.”

The announcement has drawn strong reactions from elected officials. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders are among those who have responded sharply to the policy change.
summary: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search.
author: The Verge

title: Meta staff alarmed by Muse AI privacy breaches, internal chats reveal
content:
After early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.

During testing, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.

Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.
summary: Reuters internal chats show Meta employees warned that the Muse AI agent appeared to access encrypted private messages and could mix up conversations between users. They also reported unpredictable outputs, including responses to questions staff never asked and possible exposure of sensitive information.
author: Ars Technica

title: Best Buy Restores Blu‑ray Sales Online and In‑Store
content:
Best Buy has resumed selling Blu-rays both online and in its physical stores, reversing its 2023 decision to exit the format. The retailer’s website currently lists 15 Blu-ray titles, including one two-pack, which are sold and shipped directly by Best Buy.

The available catalog features a mix of upcoming releases and classic films. New titles include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025). Older titles also available for purchase include It’s a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972).

Most of these discs can be ordered online for delivery to a customer’s address or for in-store pickup within a few days. The Odyssey is currently listed as in stock at Best Buy locations, with availability for pickup in as little as an hour.
summary: Best Buy has resumed selling Blu‑rays through its website and physical stores after ceasing sales in 2023. The site lists 15 Blu‑rays, including new releases such as The Odyssey, Project Hail Mary, Supergirl, Super Mario Galaxy, and Obsession, as well as older titles like It’s a Wonderful Life, Saving Private Ryan, and The Godfather.
author: Ars Technica

title: Windows Server 2028 Public Preview Introduces Hardened-By-Default Security for Server Core
content:
Microsoft announced the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview during its Ignite event, introducing a new security-by-default stance and a feature labeled Hardened Server Core. The upcoming server version will implement a default security framework aligned with hardened Department of Defense benchmarks, specifically referencing the Defense Information Systems Agency’s Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). This approach provides a standard security framework for system administrators, shifting the operational model from a previous state where administrators started from a blank canvas and manually implemented hardening configurations after setup.

Microsoft stated that the secure configuration is now the starting state rather than a post-setup project, a change designed to close the exposure window for newly deployed servers while they wait to be hardened. However, this hardened-by-default state is exclusively available for Server Core installations. The announcement notes that Windows Server Desktop Experience installs will not include the changed security stance.
summary: Microsoft announced the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview at Ignite, featuring a default security framework aligned with DISA STIGs. The hardened‑by‑default configuration applies only to Server Core installations, while Desktop Experience installs remain unchanged.
author: Ars Technica

title: Netflix Co-CEO Sarandos says app may bury desired content under unwanted content
content: Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos acknowledged in a Bloomberg interview that the company’s app may bury content users want to watch under material they do not. Sarandos also stated that the competition to be the top streaming company remains ongoing. Despite Netflix holding the largest subscriber base with over 325 million users as of January, he noted that audiences continue to spend significant time watching traditional broadcast television.
summary: Ted Sarandos, co-CEO of Netflix, said the company's app may bury desired content under unwanted content. He also noted that people still spend significant time watching traditional broadcast TV.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump Withdraws FDA Nominee Heidi Overton; Senate Cancels Vote on NSF Pick
content:
Trump’s administration has faced two sudden setbacks in less than 24 hours.  The White House withdrew its nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration, and the Senate has scrapped the vote on the president’s pick for the National Science Foundation.

Overton, a senior domestic‑policy aide in the White House, was nominated to head the FDA.  She has drawn criticism from both Republicans and Democrats over her positions on vaccines, abortion, vapes and birth control.  During her September confirmation hearing, she repeatedly stonewalled senators, refusing to answer questions about how she would handle the FDA’s safety review of the abortion pill mifepristone and about her stance on Trump’s statements regarding the measles vaccine and vaccine dosage.

The Senate’s decision to cancel the vote on the NSF appointment follows the same pattern of uncertainty surrounding the administration’s nominees.
summary: In less than 24 hours, Trump withdrew his nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. The Senate also scrapped a vote on his pick to lead the National Science Foundation.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ukraine collapses Kerch Bridge segment with relay drones, bypassing Starlink
content:
Ukrainian forces carried out a coordinated strike on the Kerch Strait Bridge on the nights of November 15 and 16.  A barrage of missiles and drones damaged a critical steel arch that supports the bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an update from the Institute for the Study of War.  The attack was executed deep within Russian‑occupied territory without using the military‑grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the weapons.

Russian reports said that several hundred Ukrainian drones first saturated Russian air‑defense systems, clearing the way for remote‑controlled missile strikes.  Among the missiles used was Ukraine’s home‑grown Flamingo cruise missile.  The operation employed a Russian battlefield innovation: drones fitted with mesh radios that form an airborne communications network.  Each networked drone acts as a relay node, extending the link between human operators and the remotely piloted missiles and strike drones.  Russia has used the same technique to support long‑range drone and missile attacks on Ukrainian cities.
summary: Ukrainian missiles and drones collapsed a steel arch of the Kerch Strait Bridge on November 15 and 16. The strike used relay drones with mesh radios to extend the communication link, bypassing the military‑grade Starlink system.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote
content:
The Senate Commerce Committee, chaired by Senator Ted Cruz (R‑Texas), approved the Federal Communications Commission nominee today. All 15 Republican members voted in favor of former FCC staffer Danielle Thumann, while the 13 Democrats were absent, preventing a quorum.  

The committee’s decision followed accusations that Thumann had given false testimony about her work as a legal advisor to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Despite the Democrats’ boycott, Cruz said, “We’re going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs,” and proceeded with a Republican‑only vote.  

Nominees are vetted in committees before seeking the Senate’s majority approval. Republicans hope to confirm Thumann before the Senate shifts to Democratic control in January.
summary: A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote.
author: Ars Technica

title: Nvidia Skips 10‑Q Filing, Analysts Probe Intrigue
content:
Nvidia surprised investors by announcing it would not file its formal quarterly results document, the 10‑Q, for weeks.  

A Wall Street analyst investigated the announcement and clarified the reasoning.
summary: Nvidia announced it would not file its 10‑Q for weeks. A Wall Street analyst explained the reason behind the surprise announcement.
author: TechCrunch

title: Satya Nadella: Many critical infrastructures are ‘unpatchable’ amid AI cyberattack fears
content:
Satya Nadella said lots of critical infrastructure is “unpatchable” amid fears of AI cyberattacks.  

He downplayed a recent Outlook outage and noted AI brings both opportunities and new challenges for securing the connected world.
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella downplayed the recent Outlook outage. He noted that AI is creating both opportunities and new challenges for securing much of the connected world.
author: TechCrunch

title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches after 13 years, cost over $1 billion, forecast 40 million sales
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived after 13 years in development, and the publisher is inviting players to share their initial thoughts. The release is described as potentially the most highly anticipated video game of all time.

The new installment of the crime saga is reported to have cost more than $1 billion to make and is widely expected to break sales records, with some forecasts projecting 40 million copies sold within the first three months.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI has launched after 13 years of development. The game reportedly cost more than $1 billion to make and analysts predict up to 40 million copies sold in its first three months.
author: Guardian Technology

title: PlayStation experiences widespread network issues hours before GTA VI launch
content: PlayStation experienced widespread network problems just hours before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, a title described as one of the most eagerly anticipated in recent gaming history. The disruption emerged on Wednesday, prompting a surge of complaints on social media. Players reported failed logins and difficulties connecting to servers while attempting to download games and updates. The timing of the outage coincided with the critical launch window for the highly anticipated game.
summary: PlayStation suffered widespread network problems just hours before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. The disruption led players to report failed logins and server connection problems when downloading games and updates.
author: Guardian Technology

title: MapQuest briefly tops navigation apps after defying president’s Lake Ontario order
content: After refusing to obey the president’s Lake Ontario order, MapQuest briefly rose to No 1 in navigation apps. It’s now a tool in the US anti-surveillance movement I am among the legion of former PC desk occupants with warm memories of MapQuest, the Y2K-era travel website that kept millennial drivers on course with sheaves of printed-out directions – a quantum leap over the ungainly glovebox map. But I assumed it had long since gone the way of AIM and Skype, its manual turn-by-turn guidance made obsolete by big tech. Proof of life came in January 2025, when Donald Trump issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America – a change Apple Maps and Google Maps promptly adopted, while MapQuest … did nothing. Not only had it never signed off, MapQuest was reinventing itself as a plucky oppositional hero, the app most likely to uphold your geographical beliefs.
summary: MapQuest briefly rose to No 1 in navigation apps after refusing to obey the president’s Lake Ontario order. The service has not adopted Donald Trump’s executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America, positioning itself as an anti‑surveillance, oppositional app.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Four Maryland high school students sue over AI mistake that flagged Doritos as gun
content:
Four current and former students from a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit after a police detainment incident a year ago. The students, who are football players, were handcuffed and detained by armed officers while waiting for rides home when an AI gun‑detection alert mistakenly identified a bag of Doritos as a firearm, leaving them traumatized and fearing for their lives.

The plaintiffs are suing Omnilert, the company that operates the AI system, Baltimore county police, the board of education, individual officers and the school principal. They allege unlawful detention and search caused by technological and human errors.
summary: Four Maryland high school students sue over AI mistake that flagged Doritos as gun.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump and Putin shake hands before first US‑Russia‑China trilateral summit in China
content: China’s Xi welcomed the United States and Russian leaders at the APEC summit as the three heads of state prepared for their first trilateral meeting. During the gathering, Trump shook hands with Putin and said he hoped the encounter would improve the chances of ending the war in Ukraine.
summary: China’s Xi welcomed the US and Russian leaders at the APEC summit as they prepare for their first trilateral meeting. Trump shook hands with Putin and said he hopes it could help end the war in Ukraine.
author: Euronews

title: Zelenskyy proposes 10 additional humanitarian evacuations, to discuss with US mediators
content: President Zelenskyy has proposed an additional ten humanitarian evacuations following the Oleshky operation. He did not specify the settlements involved, but said Ukraine’s delegation would present the plan to U.S. mediators. Separately, President Putin has suggested a similar evacuation in Kostiantynivka, which Ukraine says remains outside Russian control.
summary: Zelenskyy proposed ten more humanitarian evacuations but did not name the settlements. He said Ukraine’s delegation will raise the plan with US mediators, while Putin suggested a similar operation in Kostiantynivka, which Ukraine says Russia does not control.
author: Euronews

title: Police clash with Bangladeshi garment workers demanding higher minimum wage
content: Police in Bangladesh clash with garment workers demanding higher minimum wages. Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 takas (€215), up from 12,500 takas (€89), citing rising living costs eroding their purchasing power.
summary: Police in Bangladesh clashed with garment workers demanding a higher minimum wage. Workers want the monthly minimum wage raised to 30,000 takas (€215) from 12,500 takas (€89), saying rising living costs have eroded their purchasing power.
author: Euronews

title: Trump, Putin, and Xi Prepare for Historic Three‑Way Talks in China
content: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin recently shook hands, marking their first encounter since 2025. The handshake occurred as the three leaders—Trump, Putin, and Xi Jinping—prepare for historic three‑way talks in China, bringing them together in person for the first time.
summary: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping are preparing for historic three‑way talks in China. This will bring the three leaders together in person for the first time.
author: Euronews

title: Iraq Restarts 750,000-BPD Oil Pipeline to Turkey After 12-Year Break
content: Iraq has resumed pumping oil to Turkey via a pipeline after a 12‑year hiatus, aiming to bypass disruptions in the Hormuz Strait. The line, capable of moving up to 750,000 barrels per day, was closed in 2014 after attacks by the Islamic State. In August, Iraq and Turkey struck a one‑year shipment arrangement, with negotiations for a longer deal continuing.
summary: The pipeline can carry up to 750,000 barrels a day and was shut in 2014 after attacks by the so‑called Islamic State terrorist group. Iraq and Turkey agreed in August on a one‑year arrangement for shipments while talks on a longer deal continue.
author: Euronews

title: US Defence Secretary meets Delcy Rodríguez in Caracas, plans Colombia security talks
content: The U.S. Defence Secretary met with Delcy Rodríguez in Caracas. The meeting preceded a planned visit to Colombia, during which the Secretary will discuss bilateral security cooperation.
summary: The US Defence Secretary met Delcy Rodríguez in Caracas. He will travel to Colombia to discuss bilateral security cooperation.
author: Euronews

title: Bukele confirms airstrike destroyed Haitian gang leader Jeff Larose's mansion
content: Bukele confirmed that an airstrike targeted the luxury mansion of Haitian gang leader Jeff Larose. The Salvadoran president welcomed the destruction of the home. It remains unclear whether Larose was present in the building at the time of the bombing.
summary: The Salvadoran president said an airstrike destroyed the luxury home of Jeff Larose, a leading Haitian crime figure. It is not clear whether Jeff Larose was inside the building during the bombing.
author: Euronews

title: Alleged Russian agent arrested for spying on large US tech and defence firm in Palo Alto
content: An alleged Russian agent has been arrested on charges of spying on a large, publicly traded technology and defence firm that operates across the United States, including an office in Palo Alto, California. The indictment does not name the company.
summary: An alleged Russian agent was arrested for spying on a Silicon Valley technology firm. The indictment describes the firm as a large, publicly traded technology and defence company with offices across the United States, including Palo Alto, California.
author: Euronews

title: Etgar Keret says Netanyahu chooses between racism and war, no longer democratic
content:
François Picard welcomed Israeli writer and filmmaker Etgar Keret, author of The Seven Good Years, who joined the program from Tel Aviv.  

Keret said that Prime Minister Netanyahu is “seeking to remain in power, at any cost, including delegitimizing Arab parties and prolonging conflict.” He warned that “for him, it could be a never‑ending war as long as he's in power. He has no incentive to stop it,” and urged Israelis to examine how the war in Gaza was conducted, arguing that “the media as a whole ignored the war.”
summary: Etgar Keret says Netanyahu chooses between racism and war, no longer democratic.
author: France 24

title: Israeli army launches ground operation in central Gaza near Nuseirat camp
content:
The Israeli military announced the launch of a ground operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza. An AFP journalist observed Israeli tanks positioning themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp during the activity.

This rare ground operation follows inconclusive Israeli elections. Opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot is currently attempting to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his political brand on ensuring Israel's security. Daniel Whittington of FRANCE 24 reports on the developments.
summary: The Israeli military said it launched a ground operation on Wednesday in a Hamas‑controlled area of central Gaza. An AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks positioned east of the Nuseirat refugee camp during the operation.
author: France 24

title: Democrats elect Hakeem Jeffries as leader, set to become first Black House speaker
content: Hakeem Jeffries was elected by House Democrats as their leader on Wednesday, positioning him to become the first Black speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. The vote followed a sweeping Democratic victory in the recent midterm elections. Jeffries faced no declared challenger for the leadership role, though some newly elected progressive members expressed opposition that highlighted internal divisions over how the party should use its newfound power. The development was reported by France 24’s Fraser Jackson from Washington.
summary: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power.
author: France 24

title: Reconstruction starts on Limoges City Hall after fire
content:
A month after nationwide protests that turned violent, dramatic images of Limoges’ historic City Hall set ablaze have captured global attention. The fire, which destroyed the building’s interior, was widely reported and sparked international headlines.

Reconstruction work has now begun. Donations poured in after the blaze, and roughly 80 percent of the necessary funding has been secured, according to FRANCE 24’s Caitlin Brown.
summary: Reconstruction work on Limoges City Hall has begun after the building was set on fire. Donations have secured about 80 percent of the funding needed for the rebuild.
author: France 24

title: Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party
content: Senegal’s president has officially ended his political alliance with a powerful former prime minister and mentor, and Bassirou Diomaye Faye has been excluded from the ruling party. In Nigeria, all states expressed willingness to pursue the creation of their own police forces, while conflict and reduced funding are straining children’s education across parts of the continent.
summary: The political divorce between Senegal's president and the powerful former prime minister and mentor is official, with Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from the ruling party. All of Nigeria's states have shown willingness for a push to create their own police forces.
author: France 24

title: Fact-check: AI videos of Crimea bridge collapse after Ukraine strike are fabricated
content:
Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge that links Russia to occupied Crimea, causing damage to the structure. In the aftermath, several videos circulated online that depicted the bridge collapsed and suffering extensive damage.  

Fact‑checkers identified those clips as AI‑generated fabrications; some of the footage even incorporated branding that mimics a Ukrainian news agency to appear authentic. While the bridge was indeed hit and damaged, the dramatic viral videos were created with artificial‑intelligence technology, according to Vedika Bahl.
summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, causing damage. However, several AI‑generated videos depicting the bridge collapsed were fabricated, some using branding similar to a Ukrainian news agency, according to Vedika Bahl.
author: France 24

title: Limoges City Hall begins restoration after October 17 arson attack
content:
Work has begun to restore Limoges City Hall in central France after it was devastated by an arson attack during riots on October 17. An online fundraising campaign launched after the disaster has collected more than €1.7 million to support the rebuilding effort.

The same broadcast also noted the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, with gamers in Oceania among the first to experience the new installment.
summary: Work is underway to restore the city hall of Limoges, in central France, after it was devastated by an arson attack during riots on October 17. More than €1.7 million has been raised through an online fundraising campaign following the disaster.
author: France 24

title: 24‑month‑aged Comté wins top prize at World Cheese Awards
content: A 24‑month‑aged Comté, described as having a nutty flavour and a smooth, supple texture, was named the world’s best cheese after defeating more than five thousand competitors at the annual World Cheese Awards. The unpasteurised cow‑milk cheese from the Jura Mountains was aged for two years in a former military fortress in eastern France, according to FRANCE 24’s Daniel Whittington.
summary: The 24‑month‑aged Comté, an unpasteurised cow’s milk cheese from the Jura Mountains, was aged for two years in a former military fortress in eastern France. It beat more than five thousand challengers to win the top prize at the annual World Cheese Awards.
author: France 24

title: WHO warns common bacteria now highly resistant to front‑line and last‑resort antibiotics
content: The UN World Health Organization said on Wednesday that common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to both front‑line and “last‑resort” antibiotics. WHO warned the resistance situation today is worse than it was in 2019, indicating growing challenges for treating common infections.
summary: The UN World Health Organization said common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to front‑line and “last‑resort” antibiotics. It warned that the situation today is worse than it was in 2019.
author: UN News

title: COP31 deadlock continues as nations launch global climate reality check
content:
COP31 in Antalya is facing a continuing deadlock as ministers remain split on several of the conference’s most contentious issues. Delegates have not resolved questions about who should finance climate action, the pace at which the world should move away from fossil fuels, or whether a greener future can be deemed “just” when poorer nations lack the resources to afford it.

Amid the stalemate, countries announced on Wednesday the launch of a new global “climate reality check” to assess whether existing climate promises are being fulfilled. The initiative aims to provide a systematic review of commitments while negotiations remain unresolved.
summary: Countries launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept at COP31 in Antalya as the summit deadline approaches. Ministers remained deadlocked over key issues including financing, the pace of fossil‑fuel phase‑out, and the fairness of a greener future for poorer nations.
author: UN News

title: Israeli tanks cross Gaza “yellow line” in first incursion since ceasefire
content:
Israeli tanks crossed the “yellow line” boundary into Hamas‑controlled central Gaza on Wednesday, marking the first ground incursion since the fragile ceasefire agreed in October. The tanks moved along the Salah al‑Din road, Gaza’s main north‑south route, and the advance forced dozens of displaced Palestinians to leave their tents.

The operation occurred a day after the US‑backed Board of Peace, which oversees the ceasefire, said both Israel and Hamas had failed to honour their commitments to end hostilities. Meanwhile, Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Eisenkot is seeking to form a government without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
summary: Israeli tanks cross Gaza “yellow line” in first incursion since ceasefire.
author: Guardian World

title: Cheese, pet passports and youth mobility: what’s in the UK-EU ‘relationship reset’ draft?
content: A leaked 72‑paragraph second draft of the UK‑EU “relationship reset” agreement outlines provisions on topics such as cheese, pet passports and youth mobility. The document shows that most of the deal has been agreed, although a few points remain unresolved. The negotiations, which began in earnest under Prime Minister Keir Starmer, are slated for a formal sign‑off by Andy Burnham in Brussels on Friday.
summary: A leaked 72‑paragraph second draft of the UK‑EU “relationship reset” agreement shows the deal is largely reached, though some points remain outstanding. The agreement, which began under Keir Starmer, is expected to be signed by Andy Burnham in Brussels on Friday.
author: Guardian World

title: EU to halt talks on UK long‑term ties until government decides on reversing Brexit
content:
The European Union has announced it will shut the door to talks with Andy Burnham about the United Kingdom’s long‑term relationship with the bloc until the UK government decides whether to proceed with reversing Brexit. Diplomats say the piecemeal “reset” approach is coming to an end and that Europe wants clarity on whether Britain wants to reverse its exit.

European capitals have warned that they have reached the end of the line for piecemeal reset summits with the UK. They want the prime minister to focus on his next steps domestically before any further discussions can take place.
summary: The EU will shut the door to discussions with Andy Burnham about the United Kingdom’s longer‑term relationship until the government decides whether to reverse Brexit. European capitals also warned they have reached the end of piecemeal “reset” summits with the UK and want the prime minister to focus on domestic steps before proceeding.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian PM Anthony Albanese joins group photo with Vladimir Putin at APEC summit in China
content:
Anthony Albanese appeared in a leaders’ photo with Russian President Vladimir Putin at this week’s Asia‑Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. The Australian prime minister’s participation came after the Ukrainian‑supporting community in Australia urged him to protest Russia’s war.

After arriving in Shenzhen on Wednesday, Albanese said he would respect the wishes of the Chinese hosts of the summit and take part in the group picture. The decision was made despite calls from pro‑Ukraine Australians for a different stance.
summary: Anthony Albanese appeared in a leaders’ photo with Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. He said he would respect the wishes of the Chinese hosts despite urging from Australia’s Ukrainian community to protest Russia’s war.
author: Guardian World

title: GTA 6 tops Metacritic best games list with 99/100 score as Australian gamers celebrate
content: Players can renovate houses, fix cars, lift weights and follow the story in Grand Theft Auto VI’s Miami-inspired Vice City Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email Gamers across Australia woke up Thursday morning feeling like Christmas had come early, some bleary-eyed from late-night sessions on the PlayStation, others with grand plans for a weekend foray in Vice City when their day jobs let them loose. Grand Theft Auto VI, more than a decade in the making, is here. And the reviews, mere hours into release, reflect universal acclaim. The game has already vaulted to the top spot on Metacritic’s list of the best games of all time, sitting above 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with an unprecedented 99/100 score.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI lets players renovate houses, fix cars, lift weights and follow a story set in a Miami‑inspired Vice City. Within hours of release, Australian gamers gave it universal acclaim and it reached the top spot on Metacritic’s best‑games list with a 99/100 score, surpassing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
author: Guardian World

title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
content:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship, was convicted on Wednesday of US charges related to the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. Following a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami, the jury found Sanon guilty of charges that included conspiring to kill Moïse.

The defendant faced a total of eight charges, which included conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States. As a result of the conviction, Sanon now faces a potential life sentence in prison.
summary: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president.
author: Guardian World

title: Guardian readers split on Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond
content: ‘Deliciously dark’! ‘Not sexy enough’! Opinion is split on whether the star of Twilight and The Batman is the right choice to play 007. Here’s what some of you thought So it’s official, Robert Pattinson will be James Bond. The long-awaited announcement of who would be stepping into 007’s tuxedo came as a surprise, and has divided opinion, judging by the more than 700 responses the Guardian received to a callout on the topic. Readers were split on whether bosses at the franchise’s owner Amazon were right to give the role to the star of Twilight, Tenet and The Batman. Here are some of their views.
summary: Robert Pattinson has been officially announced as the next actor to play James Bond, a decision that surprised many. Over 700 Guardian readers responded to the news with divided opinions on whether he is the right choice for the role.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Josephine review: Mason Reeves shines in Sundance-winning drama about child rape witness
content:
Mason Reeves delivers an outstanding lead performance in Josephine, a drama directed by Beth de Araújo that has garnered prizes and acclaim since its Sundance premiere. The film stars Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan as Damien and Claire, a professional couple in San Francisco with a young daughter named Josephine. While the movie takes a significant swing with its high-concept ideas, the reviewer noted that some parts of the film feel contrived despite the strong acting.

The central plot unfolds when Damien takes Josephine to Golden Gate Park to play football. The father and daughter, who also enjoy watching the English Premier League, engage in play until Josephine runs ahead to a secluded spot. Damien is unable to immediately locate her, and it is in this isolated area that the eight-year-old witnesses a rape. The reviewer emphasized that the scene is not less horrifying for being filmed in a long shot and advised readers concerned about spoilers to look away.
summary: The film follows eight-year-old Josephine, played by Mason Reeves, who witnesses a rape in San Francisco's Golden Gate Park. Critics note that while the young actor's performance is outstanding, some of the film's high-concept ideas feel contrived.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Rockstar employee urges union vote after GTA 6 release
content:
Rockstar Games employee Nestor Uriarte has called for union recognition following the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. In an article, Uriarte, who works as an animation programmer at the studio in Edinburgh, stated that the team has the opportunity to make history a second time this month. He noted that a ballot is currently open for Rockstar employees to decide whether to grant recognition to the union they have built with their colleagues.

Uriarte expressed his personal support for the union, stating that he is voting yes. He cited his deep care for the team and his desire for them to continue delivering world-class games into the future as his reasons for supporting the initiative. The article frames the union recognition as a necessary step to safeguard jobs and ensure working conditions match the scale of the game, which Uriarte describes as the most anticipated release of all time.
summary: Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar's Edinburgh studio, supports union recognition following the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. He argues that securing union status is necessary to safeguard jobs and ensure the studio can continue delivering high-quality games.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Heated Rivalry fans attend 4DX screenings with water and scent effects
content:
Cineworld has introduced 4DX “extreme sensory” screenings for episodes five and six of the queer hockey drama Heated Rivalry. The show, created by Jacob Tierney and based on Rachel Reid’s Game Changers book series, is being presented in this novel format, which adds motion, wind, water, and scent effects to the viewing experience. While 4DX technology is typically reserved for high-octane action films, the cinema chain is offering fans an immersive take on the series’ romantic and erotic elements.

Fans have been attending big-screen marathons of the show over the past two weeks, with many specifically seeking out the 4DX version. Chloe, a fan wearing a black and yellow “Rozanov” jersey, stated that she cancelled her previous 2D tickets to attend the 4DX screening because she was eager to try the new format. The article notes that the sensory effects, including icy squirts and bed-bouncing vibrations, have left some viewers dizzy, with one fan jokingly hoping paramedics would be on standby for the sex scenes.
summary: Cineworld is showing episodes five and six of the queer hockey drama Heated Rivalry in 4DX, an "extreme sensory" format that includes motion, wind, water, and scent. The novel cinema experience has attracted dedicated fans, with some cancelling standard 2D tickets to attend the immersive screenings.
author: Guardian Culture

title: HBO Doc 'When a Witness Recants' Covers 36-Year Fight for Justice in Baltimore
content:
HBO’s documentary When a Witness Recants examines a 36-year struggle for justice in Baltimore, featuring producer Ta-Nehisi Coates and three subjects involved in the case. The film details the 1983 murder of 14-year-old DeWitt Duckett, who was shot in the hallway of Harlem Park junior high school by an older teenager who stole his blue satin Georgetown jacket. This incident was reported by local press as the first time a child was killed inside a Baltimore public school.

At the time of the shooting, Coates was eight years old and living in West Baltimore. He recalls perceiving the collective horror surrounding the event, which marked a rupture in his childhood view of the world. Coates stated that the experience gave him the sense that he existed in a dangerous world, a reality he felt was distinct from the rest of America. Although he initially believed the three teenage boys arrested and convicted for the murder were the correct individuals, the episode remained a foundational imprint from his past. The documentary explores how this case unfolded and the subsequent fight for justice.
summary: HBO Doc 'When a Witness Recants' Covers 36-Year Fight for Justice in Baltimore.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jimmy Kimmel likens US mass outages to a McDonald’s soft‑serve machine
content: Jimmy Kimmel likened the United States to a McDonald’s soft‑serve machine while commenting on the mass outages sweeping the country. In the same late‑night segments, hosts also discussed a proposed Trump‑Kim Jong‑un meeting, Trump’s visit to the Philippines, rising measles cases and the news that Robert Pattinson will play the next James Bond.
summary: Jimmy Kimmel compared the United States’ widespread power outages to a McDonald’s soft‑serve machine. On the same shows, hosts also discussed Trump’s planned Philippines visit, rising measles cases, a possible Trump‑Kim Jong‑un meeting, and Robert Pattinson being cast as the next James Bond.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi balances football career with modeling work
content:
Omar Sowunmi, a 31-year-old defender for Bromley, has recently embarked on a dual career that includes professional modeling. The centre-back recalls being approached on the street by a model agency employee who suggested he pursue fashion, leading him to walk for brands like Burberry and attend Milan fashion week. Despite these high-profile opportunities, Sowunmi maintains that his primary focus remains on football.

As Bromley prepares to travel to Reading to face their new manager, Karl Robinson, the team is attempting to move off the bottom of League One. Sowunmi balances the demands of lower-league football, including trips to Doncaster, with his modeling commitments in Paris. He has expressed happiness in highlighting both sides of his professional life, noting that while there are few parallels between the two worlds, he is adept in both.
summary: Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi works as a full-time professional footballer and a part-time model. The 31-year-old center-back says he met Kanye West while walking for Burberry.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carlos Alcaraz beats Daniil Medvedev in ATP Finals group stage
content: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Daniil Medvedev in the ATP Finals group stage, marking his second consecutive dominant victory. This win follows his previous match against Francis Tiafoe and all but secures Alcaraz’s advancement to the semifinals. The article notes that Alcaraz won the coin toss and chose to receive, aiming to pressure his opponent early in the match.
summary: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Daniil Medvedev in the ATP Finals group stage. This victory all but secures Alcaraz's passage into the last four.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
content:
The upcoming tender process for US television rights to the 2030 World Cup is expected to be the most competitive and expensive auction in the tournament’s history. Media rights and broadcast experts in the US and Europe anticipate that the deal will fetch between $1.5bn and $2bn, a stark contrast to the previous year’s award, which was described as a cut-price deal implemented to avoid legal action from existing rights holder Fox Sports.

This bidding war will pit the traditional broadcaster Fox against Netflix, a streamer characterized by a “whatever-it-takes” approach. Industry observers view this contest as a potential tipping point for the sports and entertainment sector, with some predicting the outcome could serve as a landmark moment for the industry.
summary: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Astronaut Reid Wiseman Becomes Mercedes F1 Ambassador After Artemis II Mission
content:
Reid Wiseman, the commander of the Artemis II mission, has become an ambassador for Mercedes’ Formula One team. This appointment formalizes a relationship that had been developing over several years. Wiseman is one of four astronauts who completed the lunar flyby in April, alongside Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.

The new ambassador brings a unique perspective to the paddock, noting similarities between flying Artemis II into lunar orbit and the F1 team’s pursuit of sporting excellence. Described as quietly spoken and thoughtful, Wiseman stands out in a sport often characterized by larger-than-life personalities and swaggering egos.

The collaboration has been welcomed by Wiseman’s daughter, Katey, who is a fan of Kimi Antonelli, the newly crowned world champion.
summary: Reid Wiseman, the commander of the Artemis II lunar flyby, has become an ambassador for the Mercedes Formula One team. His new role formalizes a relationship that had been developing over several years.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Prem Rugby launches 12-team expansion with £20m entry fee
content:
Prem Rugby has initiated its plan to expand to a 12-team competition for the 2029-30 season by formally inviting interested clubs to submit their interest by 1 February. The expansion requires a £20 million entry fee, and Chief Executive Simon Massie-Taylor is currently in the United States seeking potential investors to support the initiative.

Several clubs are expected to participate in the process. Worcester Warriors, who won last season’s rebranded Champ, and London Irish, which has signaled intentions to return to the second tier as soon as next season, are among those anticipated to apply. Additionally, the Welsh Rugby Union has sent a letter expressing a desire for clubs to join the Prem and establish an Anglo-Welsh league.
summary: Prem Rugby has asked interested clubs to apply for the 12-team expansion by 1 February, with a £20m entry fee required. Chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor is in the United States seeking investors to support the plan to add two teams for the 2029-30 competition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bancroft claims Australia team knew of 2018 sandpaper plot
content: Cameron Bancroft has revealed that the entire Australian cricket team was aware of the 2018 sandpaper incident. These explosive claims are set to increase pressure on current captain Pat Cummins.
summary: Cameron Bancroft stated that the entire Australian cricket team was aware of the 2018 sandpaper incident. These revelations place increased pressure on current captain Pat Cummins.
author: BBC Sport

title: Zverev to Defend Himself in Lawsuit Alleging Misrepresentation of Domestic Abuse Trial
content: Lawyers for world number one Alexander Zverev stated that he will defend himself against a new lawsuit. The legal action alleges that Zverev misrepresented the outcome of a domestic abuse trial.
summary: Lawyers for world number one Alexander Zverev say he will defend himself against a lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges he misrepresented the outcome of a domestic abuse trial.
author: BBC Sport

title: Alcaraz Beats Medvedev to Advance at ATP Finals
content: Carlos Alcaraz has continued his strong late-season form by defeating world number five Daniil Medvedev. This victory effectively secures his advancement at the ATP Finals, despite an earlier injury concern.
summary: Carlos Alcaraz defeated world number five Daniil Medvedev to continue his late-season winning run. The victory all but confirms Alcaraz's progress at the ATP Finals.
author: BBC Sport

title: Joint-record six referee errors in last Premier League weekend
content: The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel has identified six on-field errors during the most recent round of matches. This total represents a joint-record for the highest number of referee mistakes in a single weekend.
summary: The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel rules there were six on-field errors in the last round of games - the joint-highest in one weekend.
author: BBC Sport

title: Rassie Erasmus plans online watchalong for South Africa vs Ireland
content: Rassie Erasmus has announced plans to host an online watchalong for the upcoming South Africa versus Ireland match. Despite being described as a serial offender for criticising officials, Erasmus retains significant support within South Africa.
summary: Rassie Erasmus is a serial offender when it comes to criticising officials, but he retains huge support in South Africa. He has unique plans for following his team's game against Ireland.
author: BBC Sport

title: BBC Sport reviews who was present and what they said in sandpaper scandal
content: BBC Sport has published an analysis of the sandpaper scandal, focusing on the individuals present and their subsequent statements. This review follows explosive allegations made by Cameron Bancroft, which have generated further questions regarding the incident.
summary: BBC Sport reviews who was present and what they said in sandpaper scandal.
author: BBC Sport

title: El-Sayed calls Jeffries Medicare expansion plan 'a great start'
content: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) stated on Tuesday that he supports a Democratic proposal to expand healthcare access by lowering the Medicare eligibility age. El-Sayed characterized the plan as “a great start” in an interview with MS NOW’s Jen Psaki, noting it represents a smaller step than some progressive Democrats are advocating for with their new majority.
summary: El-Sayed calls Jeffries Medicare expansion plan 'a great start'.
author: The Hill

title: FAA chief blames outage as Duffy pushes $50B upgrade; Dems pick Jeffries speaker
content:
The Trump administration is working to address growing scrutiny of the nation’s aviation infrastructure after a series of technical disruptions, including a nationwide ground stop that halted thousands of flights last week.  

On Tuesday, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy reiterated his call for roughly $50 billion to modernize the Federal Aviation Administration as investigators continue probing the recent outages.
summary: FAA chief said he was to blame for the recent outage while Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy urged about $50 billion for FAA modernization. Democrats selected Jeffries as speaker.
author: The Hill

title: Thune to decide on Pentagon budget reconciliation within 24 hours
content: Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S. D.) aims to decide by Thursday morning whether Republicans will pursue a budget reconciliation process to fund the Pentagon. A decision may follow the GOP’s Wednesday lunch meeting, with Thune stating that a budget resolution must be passed before Thanksgiving.
summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune aims to decide by Thursday morning if Republicans will pursue a budget reconciliation to fund the Pentagon. He may make the decision after the GOP’s Wednesday lunch meeting, noting that a budget resolution must pass before Thanksgiving.
author: The Hill

title: Democrats flip 9 Senate seats, most since 1958
content: Democrats flipped nine Senate seats in this year’s midterm elections, the most since 1958, securing majorities in both chambers of Congress. According to the Associated Press, the last time Democrats gained nine or more Senate seats in a midterm election was during Republican President Dwight Eisenhower’s second term.
summary: Democrats flipped nine Senate seats in this year's midterm elections, the most since 1958. They are set to hold the majority in both chambers of Congress following a sweeping victory.
author: The Hill

title: Bob Inglis urges US to lead 35-by-35 goal via clean energy and nuclear investments
content: Former U.S. Rep. Bob Inglis argues that the United States can still lead on the 35-by-35 goal despite missing the climate change summit. He advocates for the U.S. to drive global electrification and sustainable AI infrastructure by investing in clean energy, advanced batteries, and small nuclear reactors.
summary: Bob Inglis urges US to lead 35-by-35 goal via clean energy and nuclear investments.
author: The Hill

title: Pence: Lutnick 'may need to go' over Nvidia and Huang issues
content: Former Vice President Mike Pence said he believes Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick “may need to go” following criticism over his handling of Nvidia’s sale of advanced AI technology to China and an alleged honey trapping scheme targeting the firm’s former CEO, Jensen Huang. Appearing on CNN’s “The Source” Tuesday, host Kaitlan Collins asked Pence on…
summary: Former Vice President Mike Pence stated that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick may need to go. This comment followed criticism regarding Lutnick's handling of Nvidia's AI technology sales to China and an alleged honey trap targeting Jensen Huang.
author: The Hill

title: Reporter asks SCOTUS to hear case on protecting confidential sources
content: A longtime national security reporter has petitioned the Supreme Court to hear a case concerning the protection of confidential sources. She is currently facing significant fines in a civil lawsuit due to her refusal to disclose her source's identity.
summary: A longtime national security reporter is facing steep fines in a civil lawsuit for failing to disclose her source. She is asking the Supreme Court to weigh in on the case.
author: NPR Politics

title: Trump SNAP changes require adults up to 65 to work or volunteer
content: The Trump administration has implemented sweeping changes to SNAP food aid, requiring older adults up to age 65 to work or volunteer to receive the benefit. These new work rules have disrupted the retirement plans of individuals who had left the workforce early to care for family members.
summary: The Trump administration has implemented sweeping changes to SNAP food aid. These new rules require older adults up to age 65 to work or volunteer to receive the benefit.
author: NPR Politics

title: Trump lands in China for meetings with Xi and Putin
content: President Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China, where President Xi Jinping greeted him on the tarmac. This gesture reciprocated a similar welcome Trump extended to Xi during the Chinese leader’s visit to Washington in September. Key meetings between Trump and Xi, as well as a scheduled meeting with Vladimir Putin, are on the agenda.
summary: President Trump arrived in Shenzhen, where Xi greeted him on the tarmac. This gesture reciprocated a similar honor given during Xi's visit to Washington in September.
author: NPR Politics

content: Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola has won one of the U.S.'s most watched Senate races. Separately, Nvidia's board stated it does not plan to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang, despite pressure from his allies.
summary: Former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola has won one of the U.

title: House Oversight Chair Garcia Warns 13 Trump Allies to Save Records
content: Incoming House Oversight Committee chair Robert Garcia has warned 13 Trump allies to preserve their records in anticipation of upcoming investigations. The recipients of these letters include Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Jared Kushner, and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.
summary: Incoming House Oversight Committee chair Robert Garcia sent letters to 13 Trump allies warning them to preserve records for upcoming investigations. Recipients included Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Jared Kushner, and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.
author: NPR Politics

title: Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker of the House
content: New York Democrat Hakeem Jeffries has been formally nominated as the House speaker by his party. House Democrats voted overwhelmingly to support him, moving him a step closer to becoming the first Black lawmaker in U.S. history to serve in the role.
summary: House Democrats voted overwhelmingly to support Hakeem Jeffries for speaker of the House. Jeffries, a New York Democrat, could become the first Black lawmaker to hold the position.
author: NPR Politics

title: UK Environment Regulator Says Government Breaking Law Over Wild Bird Decline
content: Populations at lowest level on record with 45% of native breeding species in decline, environment watchdog says The environment secretary, Angela Eagle, her ministers and Natural England are breaking the law by failing to intervene to slow the “deeply concerning” decline of Britain’s wild birds, the UK’s environment regulator has said. New data shows that wild bird populations have dropped to their lowest level on record, with almost half – 45% – of 132 native breeding species in decline over a five-year period.
summary: The UK's environment regulator stated that the environment secretary and Natural England are breaking the law by failing to stop the decline of wild birds. New data indicates that 45% of 132 native breeding species are in decline, marking the lowest population level on record.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Panama minister says world held hostage by oil mafia at Cop 31
content: 30 countries now signed up to forge new fossil fuel treaty, separate to UN process The world is “being held hostage by the petroleum mafia” and seems unable to break free, Panama’s environment minister has warned, as key issues remain unresolved in the final days of the UN Cop31 climate summit. “We are in love with our kidnappers,” said Juan Carlos Navarro, at a press conference to announce 30 countries were now signed up to forge a new fossil fuel treaty, separate to the UN process. “We love the petroleum guys. We can’t live without them, and they are so smart they have convinced us that they are doing this for our own good.”
summary: Panama's environment minister Juan Carlos Navarro stated that the world is being held hostage by the petroleum mafia during the final days of the UN Cop31 climate summit. Thirty countries have signed up to forge a new fossil fuel treaty separate from the UN process.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Republicans aim to fast‑track bill shielding big oil from climate lawsuits
content:
Climate groups warn that Republican lawmakers are rushing to pass a bill by the end of the year that would grant fossil fuel companies immunity from lawsuits and legislation aimed at holding them accountable for the climate crisis. This effort is part of a broader push by GOP legislators to enact high-priority bills before newly elected Democrats are sworn in following the recent election.

In response, hundreds of elected leaders and climate organizations sent a letter to congressional Democratic leadership. The group urged Democrats to reject any proposal that would shield fossil fuel companies from liability related to the climate crisis.
summary: Republican lawmakers are accelerating a high‑priority bill that would grant fossil fuel companies immunity from climate‑related lawsuits before newly elected Democrats take office. Hundreds of elected officials and climate groups have sent a letter to Democratic congressional leaders urging them to reject any proposal that shields the industry from liability.
author: Guardian Environment

title: US Offshore Windfarms Create Artificial Reefs, Transforming Ocean Floor
content: Scientists and fishers study how these ‘reefs’ and the creatures living on them are transforming the ocean floor – and what it means for the fishing industry A few years ago, Tony DiLernia, a New York-based charter boat captain, heard rumors of prime fishing near the Block Island windfarm, off the tip of Long Island. So he went with his family to see for himself. Almost immediately after motoring up to one of the project’s five turbines, black sea bass and summer flounder started nibbling at his rod and reel. DiLernia, who has fished for 50 years, wasn’t surprised: he knew about the reef effect, where certain species cluster around structures like the turbines. “It’s what we call ‘stupid fishing’,” he joked. “You’ve got this thousand-foot [signpost] sticking up out of the water saying: ‘Fish here.’”
summary: Scientists and fishers are studying how the Block Island windfarm’s five turbines create artificial reefs that attract black sea bass and summer flounder. The reef effect, where species cluster around structures like turbines, could alter the fishing industry, as noted by New York-based captain Tony DiLernia.

The study highlights a dental compound, K21, which was shown in lab tests to boost the bacteria-fighting ability of human immune cells.

Over the past two decades, the number of children and teenagers seeking help for anxiety and depression has skyrocketed, and researchers argue the increase cannot be dismissed as merely a greater willingness to discuss feelings.

Research indicates that opening new grocery stores does not increase food access in low‑income areas.  

The U. S. Department of Agriculture defines food deserts as low‑income neighborhoods where residents have limited access to healthy and affordable food. Although adding a grocery store is a common proposal, it does not guarantee that residents will shop there.

title: Dual-targeted CAR T-cell therapy shows promise in patients with treatment-resistant multiple myeloma
content:
A first‑in‑human study conducted by investigators at Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute reported that the chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T‑cell therapy TriPRIL reduced or eliminated signs of cancer in 12 of 15 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.

TriPRIL, short for trimeric APRIL (a proliferation‑inducing ligand), targets two proteins on myeloma cells rather than a single protein, offering a dual‑targeted approach.

The study results were published in The Lancet.
summary: A first-in-human study by Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute investigators found that a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy called TriPRIL reduced or eliminated signs of cancer in 12 of 15 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. TriPRIL—short for trimeric APRIL (a proliferation-inducing ligand)—recognizes two proteins on myeloma cells instead of just one.
