title: Short, frequent walks beat a single long walk in controlling blood sugar
content:
A randomized trial published in Obesity found that interrupting prolonged sitting with frequent brisk walks improves blood glucose regulation more effectively than the same amount of walking performed as a single continuous bout.  

The study indicates that multiple short walks better control blood sugar than one long walk.
summary: A randomized trial in Obesity found that interrupting prolonged sitting with frequent brisk walks improves blood glucose regulation more than the same amount of walking done in a single continuous bout. The study shows that short, frequent walks are more effective for blood sugar control.

title: Chewable fish oil emulsion yields higher omega-3 blood levels than soft gel
content: A crossover clinical trial published in the European Journal of Lipid Science and Technology found that a chewable fish oil emulsion supplement may produce higher circulating levels of omega‑3 fatty acids than a traditional soft‑gel capsule. The investigators reported the emulsion’s superior bioavailability in the study.
summary: Investigators conducted a crossover clinical trial that was published in the European Journal of Lipid Science and Technology. The trial found that a chewable fish oil emulsion supplement may provide higher circulating levels of omega-3 fatty acids compared with a soft gel.

content: A new Strategic Management Journal study by Liudmila Alekseeva, José Azar, Mireia Giné, and Sampsa Samila finds that AI adoption is associated with an increase in managers rather than a reduction. The researchers analyzed U.S. job postings from 2010 to 2022, linking firm-level AI adoption with managerial vacancies and the specific skills required for those roles.

content: On August 26, 2026, a massive rock and ice formation detached at an altitude of approximately 5,200 meters in the Himalayas. The resulting avalanche of debris and water surged toward the Nepal-Tibet border with such intensity that its seismic signals were initially misidentified as an earthquake.

content: A new model reveals how tile drainage changes water movement, affecting surface ponding, water‑table dynamics, crop growth, nutrient transport and water quality. However, fields with similar drainage can respond differently because of variations in soil, topography, and tile design—differences that most models struggle to resolve at the field scale.

title: Photon fluctuations offer new way to probe electron dynamics in crystals
content:
High-harmonic generation, a process where intense laser light causes crystals to emit new colors at frequencies much higher than the original beam, serves as a powerful method for investigating rapid electron motion in solids. While researchers typically analyze the brightness and spectrum of this emitted light, these measurements only capture a portion of the available data.

Fluctuations in the light between individual laser pulses offer an additional avenue for understanding how the emission is produced. By examining these photon fluctuations, scientists can gain further insights into electron dynamics within crystals, complementing traditional spectral and intensity-based analyses.
summary: High-harmonic generation from intense laser light produces new colors at much higher frequencies than the original beam, allowing study of rapid electron motion in solids. Researchers find that pulse-to-pulse fluctuations in the emitted light reveal additional information about the emission process beyond brightness and spectrum measurements.

title: Houston Tops Large Metros in Child Poverty and Disconnected Youth Rates
content: Houston, identified as one of the nation's largest economic engines, leads large metropolitan areas in child poverty and disconnected youth. For many of the city's youngest residents, the path to financial stability is marked by significant obstacles.
summary: Houston leads large metros in child poverty and disconnected youth. Houston is one of the nation's largest economic engines, yet many of its youngest residents face significant obstacles on the path to financial stability.

title: Study Links Climate Pressure to Rising Income Inequality in Emerging Markets
content:
A recent study published in Sustainable Development examined how climate change affects income inequality in 23 emerging market economies between 2002 and 2022. The analysis found that higher climate pressure is positively associated with income inequality measured by the Gini coefficient, the Palma ratio, and the Theil index.

The study also identified that per‑capita income and institutional quality are negatively associated with inequality, while unemployment is positively associated with it. These findings suggest that climate change may exacerbate income disparities in emerging markets.
summary: Study Links Climate Pressure to Rising Income Inequality in Emerging Markets.

title: Eagles Hunt Human-Sized Baboons, Challenging Evolutionary Defense Theory
content: Researchers from the University of St Andrews report that eagles are preying on baboons the size of hominins. This discovery challenges existing theories regarding predator–prey interactions during human evolution.
summary: Researchers from the University of St Andrews discovered that baboons the size of hominins are being preyed upon by eagles. This finding reshapes how scientists might think about predator–prey interactions during human evolution.

title: Coroner concludes Ballymacombs More Woman was decapitated over 2,000 years ago
content:
A coroner’s inquest-style inquiry has concluded that the Ballymacombs More Woman, whose Iron Age remains were discovered in a County Derry bog three years ago, was decapitated more than 2,000 years ago. The investigation into Northern Ireland’s most venerable cold case determined that the victim was a female between 15 and 22 years old at the time of her death.

The findings indicate that the woman was beheaded from behind using a bladed weapon. The inquiry suggested that she may have been ritually sacrificed, providing a formal determination on the circumstances surrounding the ancient remains.
summary: A coroner’s investigation concluded that Ballymacombs More Woman, iron‑age remains found in a County Derry bog, was a 15‑ to 22‑year‑old female. She was beheaded from behind with a bladed weapon more than 2,000 years ago.

title: Cambridge Dictionary Names 'Human' Word of the Year 2026
content: Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human. Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”.
summary: Cambridge Dictionary has chosen the word "human" as its 2026 word of the year, highlighting the importance of meaning in the age of AI chatbots. It defines "human" as having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines.

title: Viagra‑mimicking pill slows Alzheimer’s cognitive decline by a third
content:
The pill that mimics Viagra, relaxing blood vessels and increasing blood flow to the brain, was studied in a global trial. Experts called the results very promising.

The study found the medication slowed cognitive decline in people with Alzheimer’s disease by almost a third. Alzheimer’s is the most common form of dementia, with a forecast of 153 million affected worldwide by 2050, and there is currently no cure.
summary: A global study found that a pill that mimics Viagra slows cognitive decline in people with Alzheimer’s disease by almost a third. The medication relaxes blood vessels and increases blood flow to the brain.
author: Guardian Science

title: Sierra Nevada receives first major water‑year snowfall, I‑80 closed at Donner Pass
content:
California’s Sierra Nevada entered the 2026 water year with an early winter storm that arrived on 13 November. A moisture‑laden system produced heavy rain across the Sacramento lowlands and deposited roughly a foot of snow in several mountain locations. The storm marked the first of a rapid series of Pacific disturbances that have been delivering rain, snow and wind to the western United States in mid‑November.

NASA’s Terra satellite, using the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), captured a clear view of the fresh snow cover on the morning of 14 November. The image shows a stark contrast to a photograph taken two days earlier, when the Sierra peaks were largely bare and snow was confined to the highest elevations.

Ground observations reported nearly 12 inches (30 cm) of snowfall at Donner Pass, northwest of Lake Tahoe, according to the Central Sierra Snow Laboratory. The accumulation caused traffic snarls on Interstate 80, prompting officials to close the highway in both directions that evening. Further south, Mammoth Mountain ski resort recorded 9 to 13 inches (23 to 33 cm) of new snow, while Yosemite National Park closed several roads in anticipation of the storm.

The National Weather Service issued a winter‑storm warning for Sierra areas above 5,000 feet (1,500 m) for 18‑20 November. The advisory warned of travel conditions ranging from difficult to impossible, gusty winds, and potential snow depths of around 4 feet (120 cm) above 8,000 feet (2,400 m). Forecasts indicate additional wet weather and mountain snowfall through the coming days.

The imagery accompanying the story was prepared by Michala Garrison, who processed MODIS data from NASA’s EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview services. The report was written by Lindsey Doermann and references coverage from Active NorCal, CapRadio, The Weather Channel and Weather West.
summary: Sierra Nevada receives first major water‑year snowfall, I‑80 closed at Donner Pass.
author: NASA News

title: APOD November 18, 2026 features image of May 14, 2025 M1 solar flare
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 18, 2026 features a photograph of the Sun’s chromosphere, the atmospheric layer above the visible surface where temperatures rise. The image was taken through an H‑alpha filter that isolates light emitted by energized hydrogen atoms as they are expelled from the Sun during a solar flare.

The flare captured in the picture occurred on May 14, 2025 and was classified as an M1 event according to GOES satellite observations. An M‑class flare is described as moderately bright in X‑rays; such eruptions can produce radio blackouts at Earth’s polar regions and generate minor radiation storms that may affect astronauts.

The accompanying explanation notes that the Sun’s outer layers become hotter farther from its core because of energy released by swirling magnetic fields that extend through the atmosphere. When these magnetic fields twist and snap, they release light and energetic particles in the form of a flare.

Credit for the image is given to Mario Cogo, with the APOD entry edited by Keighley Rockcliffe, Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, and Cecilia Chirenti. The service is provided by the Astronomy Science Division at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, NASA Science Activation, and Michigan Technological University.
summary: The November 18 2026 Astronomy Picture of the Day displays a H‑alpha image of the Sun’s chromosphere taken during an M1‑class solar flare on May 14 2025. The flare, classified as M‑class by GOES, can cause radio blackouts at Earth’s poles and minor radiation storms that may affect astronauts.
author: NASA News

title: Tested Babyark Classic and Cybex Cloud G Pro Smart Car Seats
content: The author tested the Babyark Classic and Cybex Cloud G Pro with two kids, evaluated the extra tech benefits, and identified priorities for car seat purchase.
summary: The author tested the Babyark Classic and Cybex Cloud G Pro car seats with their two kids. They reported on how the extra technology performed and what they would prioritize when purchasing a car seat.
author: Wired

title: Tesla invites buyers to reserve personal robotaxi, prompting ownership questions
content:
Tesla has announced that it has invited a select group of buyers to reserve a personal robotaxi. The company’s move introduces a new model of vehicle access that differs from traditional ownership.  

This arrangement raises significant questions about the future of car ownership, prompting discussions about how such subscription‑style or reservation‑based services may reshape the automotive landscape.
summary: Tesla says it has invited some buyers to reserve a personal robotaxi. The arrangement raises big questions about the future of car ownership.
author: Wired

title: Over a third of Gen Z-ers rely on AI for friendship, study finds
content: Over a third of Gen Zers rely on AI for friendship, according to a Gallup report. The study also finds that young people who have online‑only friends or use AI as a social companion have higher odds of loneliness than those who do not.
summary: A Gallup report shows that over a third of Gen Z-ers rely on AI for friendship. Young people with online‑only friends or who use AI as a social companion have higher odds of loneliness than those who do not.
author: Wired

title: Instagram rolls out content protection tool to flag copycat videos
content:
Instagram has begun rolling out a new “content protection” feature for creators. According to a Meta blog post, eligible creators who enroll can use the tool to automatically detect visual matches of their original videos posted on Instagram and Facebook. When a match is found, the creator receives an alert and can decide how to respond.

Meta introduced a similar safeguard for Facebook last year to help users “safeguard” their Reels and “maintain control” over their creative work. In the Instagram version, creators are notified of matched videos and can view the number of views those copies have accumulated.
summary: Instagram is beginning to roll out a "content protection" feature that automatically scans for visual matches of creators' original videos on Instagram and Facebook. Eligible creators who enroll receive alerts about matched videos, can see the matches and decide what action to take.
author: The Verge

title: Meta AI chief shares Instagram deepfake clip of Sam Altman in mascot costume
content:
Instagram is currently populated with deep‑faked videos, and the phenomenon has reached high‑profile technology leaders. In late November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, posted a short AI‑generated clip to promote Muse, Meta’s consumer AI agent. The fabricated video shows Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly—the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse—participating in a four‑way video call.

In the clip, Altman appears dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint that mimic the mascot’s appearance. The post is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” linking the visual gag to a reference about OpenAI product discussions. The content illustrates how deep‑fake technology is being used on Instagram to create humorous, yet deceptive, portrayals of prominent executives.
summary: Instagram is filled with deepfaked content, including a short clip posted by Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang. The AI‑generated video shows Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Muse mascot Jolly on a four‑way call, with Altman dressed in a furry Jolly suit.
author: The Verge

title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
content: Model ML, a startup focused on automating investment‑banking tasks, announced a $250 million financing round. The company says its agents can grasp the full context of deals that bankers and consultants handle and automatically update financial models and presentations whenever new developments affect the analysis.
summary: Model ML announced a $250 million funding round. The startup says its agents understand deal context and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect analysis.
author: TechCrunch

title: Waymo halts nationwide freeway rides after California DMV order
content: Waymo has halted all freeway rides across the United States following an order from the California Department of Motor Vehicles. The DMV stated that Waymo’s freeway operations constitute an imminent hazard to public safety, and the imposed restrictions will remain until the company demonstrates effective corrective actions to remedy the identified deficiencies.
summary: Waymo has suspended its freeway rides across the United States following an order from the California DMV. The DMV said the operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety and that restrictions will stay until Waymo demonstrates effective corrective actions.
author: TechCrunch

title: Nvidia's startup stakes rise to $65B as Huang's exit raises deal doubts
content: Nvidia’s private‑equity stakes have risen to about $65 billion, with the portfolio’s value nearly tripling in the last nine months. The growth is attributed to Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and higher valuations of existing portfolio companies. However, Huang’s departure raises uncertainty about the company’s ability to pursue future investments.
summary: Nvidia’s private investments have nearly tripled over the past nine months, reaching about $65 billion. Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking drove the growth, but his exit puts future deals in doubt.
author: TechCrunch

title: Elton John appears at ARIA Awards to support Australian artists against AI
content: British musician backs Not AI’s To Take campaign, telling the Albanese government, ‘You have a duty to protect Australian artists and their work’ Aria awards 2026 red carpet: Tame Impala, Baker Boy, G Flip and more – in pictures Elton John has made a surprise appearance at the 2026 Aria awards to draw attention to Not AI’s To Take, a major campaign backed by the creative and media industries calling on the Australian government to protect copyright law in the face of lobbying from AI companies. Delivering a pre-recorded message at Australian music’s biggest night on Wednesday, the British singer backed the new campaign, which is calling on the Albanese government to ensure Australian artists are reimbursed and consulted by AI companies interested in using their works for AI training.
summary: Elton John made a surprise appearance at the 2026 ARIA Awards, delivering a pre‑recorded message. He backed the Not AI’s To Take campaign, urging the Albanese government to protect Australian artists’ copyright and ensure they are reimbursed and consulted by AI companies.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Apple iPhone apps disrupted on Tuesday, Apple confirms outage
content:
On Tuesday, thousands of users reported disruptions to Apple iPhone apps—including Apple Pay and iCloud—and to Google’s Gmail, according to Downdetector. Apple confirmed the outages in a statement and said they had been resolved, while Google said it had not observed internal signs of an outage.

Apple’s system‑status page at 2:30 p.m. ET listed problems with the App Store, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps and AppleCare. The incident was noted as occurring days after major Microsoft issues.
summary: Apple iPhone apps disrupted on Tuesday, Apple confirms outage.
author: Guardian Technology

title: £10m Wellcome-led study to assess UK under‑16 social media ban impacts
content: Research to look at whether ban can make meaningful change in mental health and wellbeing for under-16s Countries around the world are considering social media bans for children, but whether this would work in practice has been hotly debated. Now researchers are seeking answers through a major scientific study led by Wellcome, which will be the first of its kind. Ten research projects will explore topics ranging from children’s mental health to their sleep and physical activity, comparing factors before and after the social media ban for children under 16 is introduced in the UK in spring 2027.
summary: Researchers led by Wellcome are launching a £10m study that will be the first of its kind to examine the effects of a UK social media ban for children under 16. Ten projects will investigate mental health, sleep, physical activity and other factors before and after the ban is introduced in spring 2027.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI uncovers critical security flaw in Java, the world's third‑largest language
content: A security flaw has been identified in Java, the world’s third‑largest programming language. The bug was discovered by a tech start‑up that previously uncovered a vulnerability in PHP. Using artificial intelligence, the company pinpointed the critical software bug in Java, marking another significant finding in a widely used programming language.
summary: A tech start-up that previously discovered a PHP flaw used AI to uncover a critical software bug in Java. Java is the world's third‑largest programming language.
author: BBC Technology

title: Iran says drones hit US radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa air base
content: Iran says a drone struck the U.S. radar system at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain. The island, which had been heavily targeted earlier in the war that began in February, experienced a period of calm for weeks before an Iranian drone attack on Friday, followed by a second attack on Sunday.
summary: Iran claims its drones attacked the US radar system at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain. The first strike occurred on Friday and a second followed on Sunday after weeks of peace.
author: Euronews

title: France and Malaysia strike rare earths deal as Malaysia lifts export ban for Paris
content: France and Malaysia have agreed a rare‑earths deal, with Kuala Lumpur granting an exception to its ban on exporting raw minerals to supply Paris. The two countries are raising relations to a strategic partnership, and French President Emmanuel Macron is looking beyond China for such supplies.
summary: Malaysia is making an exception to its ban on exporting raw minerals to supply France under a rare earths deal. The agreement raises France‑Malaysia relations to a strategic partnership.
author: Euronews

title: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen ahead of trilateral summit with Trump
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen. The discussions take place a day before a first‑of‑its‑kind trilateral summit in the southern Chinese city that will also bring US President Donald Trump to the meeting.
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen. The talks come a day before a first-of-its-kind trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.

title: Mary Peltola defeats Republican to flip Alaska Senate seat
content:
Mary Peltola, a Democrat, unseated a Republican in a tight race, flipping a U.S. Senate seat in Alaska.  

With the win, Democrats will control 56 of the 100 Senate seats, giving them the power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump’s administration, and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.
summary: Mary Peltola defeats Republican to flip Alaska Senate seat.

title: Europe, Jordan explore partnership with EU Commissioner Šuica and Minister Abu Ghazaleh
content: In an exclusive Euronews interview, European Commissioner for the Mediterranean Dubravka Šuica and Jordan’s Minister of Investment Tareq Abu Ghazaleh highlighted that collaboration between European investors and Jordanian businesses can generate economic value. They described Jordan as a potential gateway for Europe into the Middle East, framing the relationship as a strategic partnership for prosperity and regional stability.
summary: European investors and Jordanian businesses can create economic value, according to European Commissioner for the Mediterranean Dubravka Šuica and Jordan’s Minister of Investment Tareq Abu Ghazaleh in an exclusive Euronews piece. They described Jordan as a potential gateway for Europe to the Middle East.

content:
Iran’s army chief Amir Hatami warned on Wednesday that Tehran would retaliate in a “more devastating” manner if the United States and its allies launched new attacks on Iranian territory.  

Earlier that day, Iran’s official IRNA news agency reported that Washington had struck Qeshm Island, causing no serious damage, while Kuwait and Bahrain said they intercepted hostile strikes. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
summary: Iran's army chief Amir Hatami said on Wednesday that Iran will retaliate in a “more devastating” manner if the United States and its allies launch new attacks on its territory. IRNA reported that Washington hit Qeshm Island without causing serious damage, while Kuwait and Bahrain said they intercepted hostile strikes.

content:
US President Donald Trump arrived in China on Wednesday in preparation for a high‑stakes trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday. The meeting will bring together Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Pinging.

The summit has drawn concern that the three leaders could determine the fate of Ukraine without input from Kyiv or Europe, and that they might pursue a division of global influence into 21st‑century spheres.
summary: US President Donald Trump arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of a trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and China's leader Xi Pinging scheduled for Thursday. The meeting has sparked fears that the three men could decide the fate of Ukraine and carve up the world into 21st‑century spheres of influence.

content: Thousands of Haitians gathered on Tuesday, urging El Salvador President Nayib Bukele to continue fighting gangs as Salvadoran troops reinforce Haiti’s security forces. Experts caution that, without a long‑term strategy to curb violence and strengthen Haiti’s police, the current public backing could shift to anger.
summary: Thousands of Haitians took to the streets on Tuesday to urge President Nayib Bukele to keep fighting gangs as Salvadoran troops bolster security forces in Haiti. summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for stronger global cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of an expected meeting with US President Donald Trump. The legislation identifies certain criticisms of Israel as examples of anti‑semitic conduct, prompting concerns that it could restrict freedom of expression and advocacy for Palestinian rights. The law, however, does not create financial penalties or criminal sanctions for violators.
summary: Italy's parliament approved a new anti‑semitism bill that lists some forms of criticism of Israel as examples of anti‑semitic conduct. The law imposes no financial penalties or criminal sanctions, though critics warn it could limit freedom of expression and advocacy for Palestinian rights.

The remarks emphasized the need for active involvement of faith and Indigenous leadership in combating hate.
summary: Religious, traditional and Indigenous leaders need to be empowered to act as full partners in preventing conflict. Speakers said this at the opening of the Muscat Plan of Action Forum in Oman on Sunday.

content:
David Lammy, a former foreign secretary who also served as deputy prime minister under Keir Starmer, has urged Andy Burnham to campaign on a promise to rejoin the EU at the next election.  

Lammy made the appeal as the prime minister prepares for a major UK‑EU summit in Brussels, saying the prime minister’s Liverpool conference speech “blew the door wide open” on the issue.

title: Australian Law Reform Commission proposes ban on commercial surrogacy, full surrogate compensation
content:
Australia’s Law Reform Commission has issued recommendations on surrogacy regulation. It proposes maintaining the ban on commercial surrogacy while allowing greater compensation for surrogates and introducing safeguards concerning the child’s legal parents. The commission also calls for a nationally consistent framework to make domestic surrogacy a viable option for prospective parents.

The body’s review aims to harmonise Australian surrogacy laws with international legal obligations and to protect human rights, with particular focus on the rights and best interests of the child.
summary: The commission recommends keeping the ban on commercial surrogacy while allowing surrogates to receive full compensation. It also calls for safeguards on legal parentage and a nationally consistent framework to align surrogacy laws with international obligations and protect the child’s rights.

title: Australian wages rise 1.1% qtr, fastest since 2023, annual gain 3.5%
content:
Australian wages rose at their quickest rate since late 2023 over the three months to September, driven by this year’s increase in minimum pay for millions of lower‑paid workers. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that the wage price index climbed 1.1 percent in the most recent quarter, taking the annual growth rate to 3.5 percent.

Despite the faster wage growth, the rise remains below the pace of inflation, which is increasing more rapidly. Economists noted that the 3.5 percent annual increase keeps the Reserve Bank of Australia on alert regarding the potential need for another interest‑rate adjustment, with some warning of a possible sixth rate rise.
summary: Australian wages rise 1.1% qtr, fastest since 2023, annual gain 3.5%.

content:
Leaked documents raise questions about whether Egypt met welfare targets required to qualify for €2.5 bn in loans. The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al‑Sisi.

title: Astronomers discover rare black holes that formed when stars failed to go supernova
content:
Gravitational wave data has identified a distinct population of black holes that may have formed when massive stars failed to undergo supernova explosions. While the standard model of black hole formation involves the collapse of a stellar core triggering a shockwave that blows away the outer layers, new research suggests some massive stars instead implode directly into black holes without a visible explosion. This finding is based on data collected by the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) and its partners, Virgo and the Kamioka Gravitational Wave Detector (KAGRA).

The study, led by Katerina Chatziioannou of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), analyzed the masses and spins of 257 black hole mergers detected by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network over the past 10 years. The team observed that a vast majority of merging black holes in the universe are approximately 10 times the mass of the sun. In their sample, 10-solar-mass black holes represented 75% of the total, indicating a common origin for this specific group. Chatziioannou stated that these results represent a connection between gravitational-wave data and the underlying astrophysics of black hole birth.

A significant and unexpected finding was the scarcity of black holes with masses between 12 and 16 times that of the sun. Isaac Legred of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign noted that while 10-solar-mass black holes are frequently observed, 14-solar-mass black holes are rare. This gap in the mass distribution suggests a specific set of internal physical processes responsible for forming the abundance of 10-solar-mass black holes. The researchers also examined the spin rates of these black holes, finding that the 10-solar-mass group possesses a distinct range of spin speeds, further supporting the hypothesis of a shared formation mechanism.

The existence of "failed supernovas" is theoretically well-supported, with scientists positing that a vast population of massive stars have imploded rather than exploded. The study notes that while there is currently no hard evidence of these events, they leave behind dark patches of sky because the stars vanish without a visible explosion. The gravitational wave data align with the idea that most binary black holes in this mass range formed from this type of stellar implosion.

The research provides a new perspective on how black holes are born in extreme environments, moving beyond the traditional narrative of supernova-driven formation. Although the data are consistent with the failed supernova theory, the team emphasizes that more research is needed to fully understand the process. The findings highlight the utility of gravitational wave observations in extracting astrophysical details that are difficult to obtain through traditional optical astronomy.

The study was published on Tuesday, November 10, in the journal Physical Review D.
summary: Gravitational waves have revealed a population of black holes that may have been born when masssive stars failed to go supernova. Most of us know the origin story of black holes, or we thought we did.
author: Space.com

title: British startup Foundational tests laser retroreflector in orbit
content:
A London-based startup named Foundational has demonstrated a new technology designed to address the growing issue of space debris. According to the European Space Agency (ESA), millions of pieces of space debris currently circle Earth, posing potential dangers due to the high speeds at which objects travel in orbit. While experts have proposed various solutions, including large space nets, laser ablation, and deliberate deorbiting of large satellites, Foundational has introduced retroreflectors as an alternative approach to tracking and managing orbital objects.

The company recently completed an early-stage orbital test of its Retro-2 laser retroreflector system, which was developed in collaboration with ESA. The primary objective of the test was to verify that the device could return laser-ranging signals from a satellite operating at altitudes between approximately 600 kilometers and 870 kilometers (about 370 to 540 miles). The long-term goal of this technology is to create a tracking device that allows spacecraft to be monitored in orbit even after they cease transmitting data.

Foundational stated that the Retro-2 system requires no electronics, power, or commands from its host spacecraft, enabling ground stations to maintain tracking of orbiting objects. The demonstration mission launched in July on SpaceX’s Transporter-17 rideshare flight. For the test, the Retro-2 device, a miniaturized unit containing seven reflectors, was attached to a small satellite integrated into an ION carrier craft operated by the Italian company D-Orbit.

During the mission, the Retro-2 device successfully returned 6,111 laser shots beamed from the ground across five passes in low Earth orbit. Dave Gooding, Foundational’s co-founder and chief technical officer, noted that the tests demonstrated a device weighing just 50 grams (1.8 ounces) could deliver millimeter-level ranging precision. Gooding emphasized that as space becomes increasingly crowded, maintaining trackability of satellites throughout their lifetime and beyond is critical for managing collision risks.

Founded in 2025, Foundational recently emerged from stealth mode last month. Despite its early stage, the company has raised £8.2 million ($10.9 million) in pre-seed funding. It joins a broader group of companies involved in debris removal, satellite servicing, and debris tracking that have secured funding in 2026, including Starfish Space, which raised over $100 million in a Series B round, Katalyst Space, which received $12 million, and international firms such as India’s Cosmoserve Space.
summary: Foundational, a British startup founded in 2025, successfully demonstrated its Retro‑2 laser retroreflector system on a satellite launched in July on SpaceX’s Transporter‑17 rideshare flight. The 50‑gram device returned 6,111 laser shots over five passes in low Earth orbit, delivering millimeter‑level ranging precision without power or commands from its host spacecraft.
author: Space.com

title: Voyager 1 to reach light-day distance in 2025; Voyager 2 expected in 2035
content:
On November 18, NASA’s Voyager 1 will reach a distance of 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers) from Earth, a point where it will take a full light-day, or 24 hours, for a signal to travel to the spacecraft. This milestone is significant because light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe. In contrast, Voyager 2 is not expected to reach the same light-day distance until approximately 2035. NASA plans to celebrate Voyager 1’s achievement by inviting fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky.

The disparity in arrival times stems from trajectory decisions made during the first phase of the missions, which launched about two weeks apart in 1977 with Voyager 2 going first. Although both spacecraft were originally intended to observe Jupiter and Saturn, their paths diverged after that. Voyager 1 was placed on a faster trajectory to overtake Voyager 2 on the way to Jupiter, arriving on March 5, 1979, four months before Voyager 2 reached the planet on July 9, 1979.

Following their encounters with Jupiter, both spacecraft utilized gravity assists, a technique that allows them to gain speed by taking a small amount of momentum from the planet without significantly affecting the planet itself. According to the Planetary Society, each Voyager gained about 10 km/s (6.2 miles/s) during the 1979 Jupiter encounter. This boost was sufficient to place them on a fast path to Saturn and, for Voyager 2, eventually to Uranus and Neptune.

Voyager 1’s path included a turn at Saturn to examine the planet’s rings and the moon Titan, after which it flew outside the plane of the solar system. Voyager 2, however, continued to Uranus and Neptune to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment. During its Neptune encounter, Voyager 2 made a turn to fly by the moon Triton, which required the spacecraft to plunge down out of the plane of the solar system, resulting in a loss of speed. The Planetary Society noted that Voyager 2 gained about 10 km/s at Jupiter, 5 km/s at Saturn, and 2 km/s at Uranus, but lost about 2 km/s at Neptune.

These varying speeds explain why Voyager 1 is currently zooming out at 3.5 astronomical units per year, while Voyager 2 travels at a slower pace of 3.1 astronomical units per year. The different trajectories allowed both spacecraft to eventually reach interstellar space, with Voyager 1 arriving in 2012 and Voyager 2 in 2018. As both probes continue their journeys, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory is managing their power supplies to maximize scientific return, with the spacecraft potentially operating into the 2030s.
summary: Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference?
author: Space.com

title: The Fantasticks makes Broadway debut in gay reimagining
content:
The Fantasticks, the world’s longest-running musical, has arrived on Broadway for the first time in a new production at Hayes Theater in New York City. Originally written by Tom Jones and Harvey Schmidt, the show ran for more than 40 years off-Broadway. This new version reimagines the classic story by changing the gender of the central characters, presenting a gay courtship instead of the original heterosexual romance.

In this adaptation, the young lovers are Matt, played by Maxim Chlumecky, and Lewis, played by Nathan Levy. The production also switches the meddling parents from fathers to mothers. Leslie Rodriguez Kritzer plays Mildred, a flower gardener, while Ruthie Ann Miles plays Bessie, an avid vegetable grower. These character changes introduce additional female voices to the chamber piece, which has been described as enduringly winsome, though some may find it cloying.

Director-choreographer Christopher Gattelli leads a lively and wistful new production that retains the musical’s original structure. The show first premiered in 1960 and continues to tell the story of young lovers secretly pushed toward one another by their parents. While the genders of the main characters have been updated, the musical’s quaint attitudes about love, marriage, and childhood remain largely unchanged from the original era. The review describes the new version as a heartwarming delight for audiences seeking a sweet and whimsical romantic story.
summary: The Fantasticks, the world's longest-running musical, is receiving its first-ever Broadway run at Hayes theater in New York City. The production reimagines the original heterosexual romance as a courtship between two men and swaps the fathers for mothers.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Chilean director Sebastián Lelio dies aged 52
content: Actor Elaine Cassidy, composer Matthew Herbert and writer Rebecca Lenkiewicz pay tribute to the extraordinary talents of the acclaimed Chilean director, who has died aged 52 Elaine Cassidy, actor, The Wonder

title: Former UNO guard Jah Short sentenced to one day in prison for point-shaving
content: A federal judge has sentenced former New Orleans University guard Dyquavion "Jah" Short to one day in prison and two years of supervised release. Short is the first player to receive a sentence in a college basketball point-shaving case.
summary: A federal judge sentenced former New Orleans University guard Dyquavion "Jah" Short to one day in prison. He also received two years of supervised release for his role in a college basketball point-shaving case.

title: Clemson coach Dabo Swinney confident of more wins after rough patch
content: Clemson coach Dabo Swinney expressed confidence that he and the Tigers have many more victories ahead, despite acknowledging a self-described "rough patch" over the last two seasons.
summary: Clemson coach Dabo Swinney says he and the Tigers have many more wins ahead. He acknowledges the team has been through a rough patch over the past two seasons.

title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
content:
A new documentary titled The Match explores the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina, aiming to present the historic clash from fresh perspectives for a new generation. The film, directed by Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco, is based on Andrés Burgo’s book of the same name. At the London film festival premiere, producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo recounted how she secured the participation of Gary Lineker by showing him a 1981 image of Diego Maradona wearing a Union Jack T-shirt alongside Freddie Mercury in an Argentina strip. This “rock’n’roll angle,” which features Brian May as a talking head, is one of the few details the filmmakers added to the source material.

The 91-minute documentary, a duration matching the length of the actual match, employs a non-linear narrative that shifts between past and present. It combines anecdotes that have become part of Argentine football folklore with extensive archive footage. The film seeks to revisit the drama of the encounter, offering a re-examination of the events through this unique structural and thematic approach.
summary: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Zverev beats Shelton in ATP Finals group stage
content:
World No. 1 Alexander Zverev defeated Ben Shelton 6-2, 7-6 (4) in a straight-sets victory during the ATP Finals group stage. The match served as a rematch of the US Open final earlier this year. In the same round, Arthur Fils recovered from a deficit to secure a win against Rafael Jódar.

Pre-match commentary noted that Shelton’s backhand was effective against Fils in his initial match. The analysis suggested that if Shelton utilized that shot effectively, his chances of winning would improve, noting that his coach, Juan Carlos Ferrero, would need to address the issue to help him advance in the tournament.
summary: World No. 1 Zverev defeated Shelton 6-2, 7-6 (4) in a rematch of the US Open final. Arthur Fils also came from behind to beat Rafael Jódar in the group stage.
author: Guardian Sport

title: JJ Gabriel confirms Manchester United exit after registration cancellation
content: Teenager says ‘thank you for everything’ in video Gabriel expected to join Real Madrid JJ Gabriel has announced his departure from Manchester United by posting a farewell message to the club on social media. The teenager, who has not played a competitive game for the first team, joined as a 10-year-old in 2020 but has been absent since he requested the cancellation of his registration in September before he turned 16, on 6 October.
summary: JJ Gabriel announced his departure from Manchester United via a farewell video on social media. The teenager, who joined the club in 2020, has been absent since requesting the cancellation of his registration in September.

title: Devenny's late volley lifts Northern Ireland to Nations League top tier
content:
A late volley from Justin Devenny secured a 1-1 draw for Northern Ireland against Hungary, earning the team top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the competition’s top tier. The Stoke player struck the ball from the edge of the area to equalize, preventing Hungary from leapfrogging Michael O’Neill’s side in the standings with a victory.

Northern Ireland had trailed 1-0 following a 35th-minute goal by Barnabas Varga. The Hungarian striker slotted home from a one-on-one situation with goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive error. This goal ended Northern Ireland’s record of not conceding during the current campaign and temporarily moved Hungary to the top of the group in the live standings.
summary: Justin Devenny scored a late volley to draw Northern Ireland 1-1 with Hungary, securing top spot in Group B2. The result earned Northern Ireland promotion to the top tier of the competition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Portugal's new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied
content:
Portugal secured their first victory in the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era with a dramatic win over Wales, highlighted by a decisive goal from substitute Carlos Forbs. Forbs, who wears the new No 7 jersey featuring a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s legacy, delivered a sumptuous finish to clinch the result. The match was marked by controversy when Portugal’s Pedro Neto was sent off after receiving two yellow cards, yet the team managed to survive the remainder of the game.

For Wales, the defeat means they will face a Nations League relegation playoff double-header in March. A draw in Switzerland on Friday will determine their opponent, which could be Slovenia, Hungary, the Republic of Ireland, or Bosnia and Herzegovina. The latter had previously knocked Wales out of World Cup qualifying earlier this year.

Following the match, Wales manager Craig Bellamy emphasized the importance of remaining in the elite tier to accelerate the team’s improvement. He also confirmed that he will not continue in his role beyond Euro 2028, as his contract expires after that tournament.
summary: Carlos Forbs scored the winning goal for Portugal, a result secured despite Pedro Neto's sending-off for two yellow cards. Wales manager Craig Bellamy stated he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, as his contract expires after that tournament.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rassie Erasmus faces new ban for criticizing match officials
content:
Rassie Erasmus, the head coach of the South African Springboks, has received another lengthy ban from World Rugby for criticizing match officials. This sanction marks exactly five years since he first faced disciplinary action for similar comments. The article characterizes Erasmus as a habitual offender whose latest intemperate remarks were a "deserved" result of his lack of statesmanship, diplomacy, and good grace in defeat.

While some supporters view his outspoken nature as a key trait of his leadership, others criticize him for his repeated conduct. The piece acknowledges the remarkable achievements of Erasmus and his double World Cup-winning teams, stating that these accomplishments are widely respected. However, it argues that his behavior in defeat remains a significant disappointment, suggesting that the South African rugby program deserves better conduct from its head coach.
summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has received another lengthy ban for intemperate comments criticizing match officials. The article argues that despite the Springboks' remarkable achievements, Erasmus lacks statesmanship and good grace in defeat.
author: Guardian Sport

title: PFA head Maheta Molango warns 'the game is in danger' over Fifa and Infantino
content: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money.
summary: PFA chief executive Maheta Molango states that football is in danger because its future is being determined by profit rather than maintaining popularity. She criticizes the Folarin Balogun affair as scandalous while discussing wider fears regarding the sport's future.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jordan Cox rejects T20 rest, says he'll play for England if selected
content: Wicketkeeper-batter could have represented Australia but was destined to play for his country of birth after watching the 2010-11 Ashes at 10 In an era of sardine tin schedules and franchise teams hoping to turn heads, it was refreshing to hear Jordan Cox at the beautiful Bellerive Oval and state how desperate he is to play for England as much as is humanly possible. When the squads for this Australia tour were being discussed, the selector Marcus North gave the wicketkeeper-batter the option to sit out the Twenty20 leg before taking on South Africa’s imposing Test attack next month. Cox, recently handed a two-year central contract after a breakout summer, was having none of it.
summary: Selector Marcus North offered wicketkeeper‑batter Jordan Cox the option to sit out the Twenty20 leg of the Australia tour. Cox, who has just received a two‑year central contract after a breakout summer, declined, saying he will be there for England if they want him.

content: Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott scored two goals in a victory over Kosovo, marking a transformative year for both his club and country. The talisman’s performance capped a successful twelve-month period.

content: The White House confirmed Tuesday night that it withdrew the nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). summary: The White House confirmed Tuesday night that it withdrew the nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration. This decision came amid opposition from Senate Republicans, who held only a one-vote majority in the Senate health committee.

title: Guardian: Climate debt traps poor nations, undermining Cop31 climate goals
content:
The Guardian editorial argues that the international financial system is trapping poor nations in a cycle of debt that hinders their ability to prepare for climate disasters, a situation it urges the world to address at Cop31. The piece cites the August catastrophe in Nepal, where a collapsing glacier triggered deadly floods that killed thousands and destroyed infrastructure. The disaster resulted in the loss of a tenth of Nepal’s electricity generation, with reconstruction costs estimated at $5bn. However, the Loss and Damage Fund has allocated only $20m to Nepal, a sum representing less than 5% of the $482m the country must pay to external public creditors this year.

Nepal’s delegation to the UN climate conference stated that the scale of resources needs to increase, joining other nations calling for change. The editorial references ActionAid’s September report, Debt Fuels the Climate Crisis, which notes that the global south’s external borrowing is 100 times greater than the climate finance it receives. According to the charity, poor nations are trapped in debt dependency because they export cheap raw materials while importing expensive food, fuel, and manufactured goods priced in dollars. ActionAid further warned that climate-vulnerable countries are expected to fund decarbonization while servicing dollar loans that often pressure them to export fossil fuels rather than invest in green industrialization.
summary: The Guardian argues that poor countries face a vicious cycle where debt servicing costs, such as Nepal's $482m external payments, far exceed available climate disaster funds. ActionAid reports that the global south's external borrowing is 100 times greater than the climate finance it receives, trapping vulnerable nations in dependency.
author: Guardian Environment

title: UK could miss net‑zero targets if EV sales rules are weakened, CCC warns
content:
Analysts warn that a proposed relaxation of the UK’s electric‑vehicle sales rules could derail the country’s net‑zero plan. The Climate Change Committee (CCC) analysis suggests that allowing more petrol and diesel cars to be sold would create a “hole” in the strategy to reach net‑zero carbon emissions by 2050, potentially causing the government to miss legally binding climate targets.

The CCC’s findings raise concerns that the current administration, led by Andy Burnham, may need to reduce the UK’s carbon‑budget targets to compensate for the weakened electric‑vehicle policy. The advisers tracking Britain’s progress to net zero see the policy change as a significant threat to the country’s long‑term emissions‑reduction commitments.
summary: The Climate Change Committee warns that weakening the UK’s electric‑car sales rules would probably cause the government to miss its legally binding climate targets. The analysis says the change could undermine the plan to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 and may force Andy Burnham’s government to cut its carbon‑budget targets.

title: UK health test claims largely unsubstantiated, study finds
content: An assessment of 50 commercial test vendors, published in the journal BMJ Open, found that many claims regarding the benefits of health tests marketed to UK consumers are unsubstantiated. The study also noted that these vendors provide little information about the potential harms and limitations of their products.
summary: An assessment of 50 commercial test vendors found that many claims for health tests marketed to UK consumers are unsubstantiated. The study also noted that these vendors provide little information on the potential harms and limitations of the tests.

content: A small exploratory study published in BMJ Nutrition Prevention & Health found that appetite-suppressing drugs, including Wegovy and Mounjaro, are associated with inadequate intake of key nutrients and energy in some individuals.

content: Thanksgiving is approaching, a US federal holiday traditionally marked by gatherings with family and friends. title: Judge extends Trump's deposition deadline in $10bn BBC lawsuit to Jan 22
content:
Donald Trump has received a temporary extension in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC, moving his deposition deadline to 22 January. Federal magistrate judge Enjoliqué Lett originally set a firm 11 December deadline for Trump to sit for a deposition by BBC lawyers. The judge had previously warned that failure to comply by that date could result in penalties up to the dismissal of the case.

Trump had initially agreed to appear for the deposition in October but subsequently backed out. The new deadline grants him additional time before he must provide his witness statement in the legal dispute with the British broadcaster.

title: Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang
content: Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster. Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the ouster of Huang over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with his own employees.
summary: Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.84 billion, doubling from the same period a year ago. The chairman stated the company does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following his ouster.

content: Scientists are investigating how a changing atmosphere impacts the base of the ocean food chain. While concerns about elevated carbon dioxide often center on global warming, up to 30% of emitted carbon dioxide is absorbed by the oceans. This absorption reacts with water to lower pH levels, causing ocean acidification that significantly affects the chemistry and biology of marine ecosystems.
summary: Up to 30% of emitted carbon dioxide is absorbed by oceans, where it reacts with water to lower pH. This process leads to ocean acidification, which has enormous effects on the chemistry and biology of marine ecosystems.

content:
A recent study tracks what students learn from online teamwork and fieldwork abroad. The research examines how international collaboration influences students’ understanding of sustainability issues.

The study uses the example of a food‑waste reduction solution developed in Tokyo and its potential application in Seoul. By working with peers abroad, students are encouraged to question assumptions they hold at home and to consider how their knowledge might address real‑world sustainability challenges. Educators who design international courses aim to understand what students take away from the experience and what knowledge remains with them after the course ends.
summary: The study investigates whether a food waste solution effective in Tokyo can be applied in Seoul by having students work with peers abroad to challenge assumptions and apply sustainability knowledge. title: NASA Launches Power to Explore Student Contest on Lunar Nuclear Power
content:
NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge officially launched on Tuesday, November 17, inviting kindergarten through 12th grade students across the United States to participate in a science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) competition. The challenge focuses on space nuclear power systems, asking students to learn about these technologies and illustrate how nuclear “batteries” could assist in powering their vision for lunar exploration. In addition to visual work, participants are required to write a short essay describing a personal “superpower” that would aid a mission. Submissions for the 2026-2027 cycle are due by March 1, 2027.

The initiative highlights the critical role of power sources in space missions, particularly in the harsh conditions of the Moon, which include freezing temperatures, long nights, and deep craters devoid of sunlight. Carl Sandifer, a program manager for NASA’s Space Reactors Division at the agency’s headquarters in Washington, stated that establishing a lunar base requires infrastructure to support human life and research. He noted that nuclear power could enable exploration in the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon’s South Pole, transport robust science payloads over long distances, and maintain instrument warmth during the lunar night. Sandifer added that the challenge prepares the next generation of explorers to design their own nuclear-powered Moon bases.

Entries for the contest consist of a 200-word essay and an original illustration. The essay must describe one unique power the student possesses that will help the mission, while the illustration must convey a vision of a nuclear-powered lunar base supporting both human and robotic exploration. The artwork should demonstrate an understanding of how radioisotope and fission-based power solutions enable exploration. Judges will evaluate the submissions in three distinct grade-level categories: K-4, 5-8, and 9-12.

One grand prize winner from each grade category will receive a trip for two to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, where they will learn about the personnel and technologies that enable NASA missions. Additionally, every student who submits an entry will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts. This event is designed to teach participants about what energizes the NASA workforce to advance missions and sustain America’s leadership in space.

NASA and Future Engineers are currently seeking volunteers to judge the anticipated thousands of contest entries. U.S. residents older than 18 who are willing to commit approximately three hours of their time can register to judge through the Future Engineers website. The Power to Explore Student Challenge is funded by the NASA Science Mission Directorate and operates under the Radioisotope Power Systems Program within the Research and Technology Mission Directorate. Future Engineers administers the challenge through a contract with the NASA Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation.
summary: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17.

title: StarSling Launches AI‑Powered CI Runners to Cut Costs and Speed Up Workflows
content:
StarSling, a Y Combinator P25 company founded by Yonas and Daniel, has launched a platform designed to provide self-improving continuous integration (CI) for repositories with high agent volume. The service offers fast GitHub Actions runners equipped with AI agents that generate pull requests to continuously optimize tests and workflows. Each CI job operates within its own ephemeral sandbox on Zen 5 machines and NVMe disks, featuring unlimited concurrency to allow bursts of agent pull requests to run simultaneously. Unlike other runners, StarSling’s infrastructure includes agents intended to reduce CI costs over time by generating optimizations through a dedicated CI harness.

The company highlights specific performance improvements achieved with its clients. Mastra, a user of the platform, now merges over 1,800 pull requests a month and saw its slowest workflow reduced from 29 minutes and 56 seconds on GitHub-hosted runners to 5 minutes and 06 seconds on StarSling, a 5.87x speedup. Additionally, StarSling agents identified an 11-month-old performance bottleneck in the better-auth project, resulting in a fix that made one of its test jobs 5.4x faster. The founders, who previously worked on StackShare and Netflix’s internal developer portal, developed StarSling after encountering CI bottlenecks while building AI agents for DevOps, where their own agents generated so many pull requests that job queues backed up for hours.

StarSling’s CI harness runs an agent loop that analyzes workflows, run logs, and machine telemetry to propose optimizations. The system tests the unchanged workflow side-by-side with the proposed change and uses a deterministic judgment to ensure the difference is statistically significant before shipping the winner as a pull request with benchmark evidence. The company reports that benchmarking open-source repositories on its runners yields an average 10x speedup in wall-clock time with 70% less runner time. Specific benchmarks include a 12.8x speedup for gogs, 5.5x for shellcheck, 3.9x for chatwoot, 11.7x for transfer.sh, and 36.4x for mirotalksfu.

To address infrastructure costs, the team initially built runners on AWS but found them too expensive. They subsequently convinced several sandbox providers to adopt Zen 5s and began publicly benchmarking them. StarSling now supports per-second billing and has released StarSling Disks, a feature providing persistent disks that offer a 4.9x speedup in dependency readiness compared to actions/cache. The company has also released skills for users who wish to perform these optimizations themselves using prompts, though StarSling argues that using their agents saves users from expending tokens and CI compute to find optimizations independently.

StarSling has converted CI optimization strategies from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Linear into playbooks for agents. Users can access the platform via a provided documentation URL and receive 2,000 free minutes, with agents beginning to open pull requests once usage reaches approximately 10,000 minutes. The company has also announced a CI Challenge, offering a $1,000 reward if StarSling fails to save at least 10% on a user’s next CI bill. The launch post includes links to benchmarks, a demo of the disk feature, and the rules for the challenge, inviting feedback on the headless experience.
summary: We’re Yonas and Daniel and we’re building StarSling ( https://starsling. Dev ), fast GitHub Actions runners with AI agents that ship PRs to continuously improve your tests and workflows.

content:
Backrooms, originally a 4chan meme, has evolved into a cultural touchstone that draws audiences to cinema.  

An online sketch‑comedy creator, whose early work sparked the meme’s popularity, has also helped bring viewers back into theaters—an effort that signals the beginning of a broader shift in film consumption.

content: US Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin have introduced legislation to make it easier for families to sue if their child has been harmed through the massive gaming platform.
summary: US Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin introduced legislation to make it easier for families to sue if their child has been harmed through the massive gaming platform Roblox. The legislation follows a Senate hearing that slammed Roblox over child sex abuse.

title: Nike’s new air sole technology can mix soft and firm cushioning
content:
Nike is introducing Tuned Air technology, which allows for the production of air-filled soles with varying levels of cushioning and stability. This new manufacturing process creates multiple air pockets within the sole, moving away from the previously uniform cushioning found in traditional Nike Air shoes. The approach mirrors the company’s 2024 launch of the Air Max 1000, which utilized 3D printing to achieve a uniform silhouette with distinct areas of support and flexibility.

This innovation builds on Nike’s nearly 50-year history of incorporating air pockets into footwear to enhance comfort and cushioning. By enabling a mix of soft and firm zones, the Tuned Air system offers a more tailored experience compared to older, consistent sole designs.
summary: In 2024, Nike announced its Air Max 1000, manufactured with a 3D‑printing process that creates a uniform silhouette while varying support and flexibility. Nike’s new Tuned Air technology produces multiple air pockets with differing cushioning levels, replacing the previous uniform cushioning across the sole of Nike Air shoes.

title: Nvidia CEO Colette Kress reports Q3 earnings; board rejects reinstating Jensen Huang
content:
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, omitting any mention of former CEO Jensen Huang or the circumstances of his departure, or a possible return.  

During the earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones opened by stating the board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO and that questions about Jensen’s resignation or the ongoing investigation would not be addressed. Kress then presented the results.
summary: Interim CEO Colette Kress announced Nvidia's Q3 earnings on Tuesday without mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang. Board chair Harvey Jones said the board will not reinstate Huang as CEO and will not address his resignation or the ongoing investigation during the call.
author: The Verge

title: MacBook Neo gets $50 discount at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target ahead of Black Friday
content:
The MacBook Neo is currently available for $50 off at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, a discount applicable to both storage configurations and all four color options. The 256GB model is priced at $649, while the 512GB version with Touch ID is reduced to $749. None of the retailers have specified an end date for the promotion, which represents the largest price drop since Apple increased the laptop’s MSRP by $100 in July due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Apple’s budget-friendly laptop utilizes the A18 Pro processor, a chip originally designed for the iPhone 16 Pro, to maintain lower costs. Both the 256GB and 512GB models include 8GB of memory. While the device is not highly performant regarding storage speed and total memory, it is well-suited for everyday tasks, casual use, and students. A Verge colleague noted that the vivid 13-inch screen and speakers are superior to those found in many cheap and midrange Windows laptops.
summary: The MacBook Neo is discounted by $50 at several retailers, with the 256GB model priced at $649 and the 512GB model at $749. This is the largest price drop since Apple raised the laptop's MSRP by $100 in July due to the ongoing RAM crisis.
author: The Verge

title: Nvidia board says it will not reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang
content:
Harvey Jones, the new chair of Nvidia’s board, stated during Tuesday’s quarterly earnings call that the board unanimously accepted the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang and does not intend to reinstate him. Jones further announced that the company would not address questions regarding the circumstances of Huang’s resignation or any ongoing investigation during the call.

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang publicly expressed a desire to return. In a statement posted on X, he admitted that he did not live up to the company’s standards, expressed regret for his mistakes, and indicated that he would cooperate with the process.
summary: Nvidia's new board chair Harvey Jones confirmed that the board accepted former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and will not reinstate him as CEO. Huang had earlier floated a return but said he did not meet company standards, regretted his mistakes, and would cooperate with investigations.
author: The Verge

title: iFixit Finds Apple HomeView Hub Hard to Repair in Teardown
content:
iFixit’s teardown of Apple’s new HomeView hub reveals a device that is significantly more difficult to repair than recent iPads and HomePods. Despite the hub’s resemblance to a seven-inch tablet attached to a smart speaker, iFixit’s technicians encountered substantial challenges during disassembly. The process resulted in a ripped connector, a snapped speaker, and excessive force applied to the logic board, indicating that the device’s internal construction is far less repair-friendly than previously expected.

The tablet section of the HomeView presented the greatest difficulty due to specific design choices by Apple. While iFixit initially anticipated an easy disassembly similar to other recent Apple products, the actual teardown proved to be a demanding task for even skilled technicians.
summary: iFixit’s teardown of Apple’s HomeView hub revealed significant repair challenges, including a ripped connector, a snapped speaker, and damage to the logic board. The tablet section proved especially difficult to disassemble due to questionable design choices.
author: The Verge

title: Jeff Bezos says he was heavily involved in picking new James Bond
content:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos stated that he was “heavily involved” in casting Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World conference, Bezos described a rigorous selection process that began with a large group of candidates, which was narrowed down to five finalists. The team then conducted traditional screen tests for these five individuals before making the final decision on a Friday.

The announcement follows the recent confirmation of Pattinson’s role in the franchise, a move that aligns with his previous collaborations with director Denis Villeneuve, who is set to direct the next film for Amazon. Bezos emphasized the structured approach taken by the production team to finalize the choice for the iconic 007 character.
summary: Jeff Bezos stated at the Semafor conference that he was heavily involved in the final decision to cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond. Bezos described a tight process that involved down-selecting candidates to five finalists who then underwent screen tests.
author: The Verge
